1495f339f11e42e5: KUALA LUMPUR: The benchmark index FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI is expected to remain volatile amid geopolitical risks, domestic political uncertainties and inflationary pressures, as a global technology stock sell-off weighs on investor sentiment despite resilient domestic economic fundamentals.

Affin Hwang Investment Bank head of research Loong Chee Wei expects the benchmark index to face continued volatility, with elevated global bond yields and uncertainty surrounding United States policies posing risks to financial markets.

The caution comes after a sharp overnight sell-off on Wall Street spilled over into Asian markets on Friday, amid concerns that the Democratic Party's victory in the US midterm elections could lead to tighter regulatory scrutiny of artificial intelligence (AI) and slow the expansion of data centres.
The Nasdaq fell 5.5 per cent, wiping out about US$3 trillion in market value from S&P 500 companies, while Japan's Nikkei plunged six per cent.
South Korean and Taiwanese benchmark indices also fell more than eight per cent at one point during early trading.
The sell-off was also felt locally, with the KLCI falling as much as 23.53 points, or 1.4 per cent, to 1,612.33 before recovering slightly to 1,613.85 at the noon break on Friday.
Technology stocks recorded the steepest declines among Bursa Malaysia's sectoral indices, reflecting concerns over potentially tighter US regulations on the AI industry.

Loong identified geopolitical developments as a key risk, particularly uncertainty surrounding US government policies on AI and data centres, which could have wider implications for global technology companies and their supply chains.
"This has led to a sharp correction in technology company share prices that have led the global equity market performance this year," he said.
Domestically, investors are also expected to monitor developments ahead of the Melaka state election on November 14.

Nevertheless, Loong said Malaysia's economic and corporate earnings fundamentals remained supportive of the KLCI at current levels, although a sustained rebound would depend on global market sentiment and foreign fund flows.

He described Malaysia as a relative safe haven in the region, citing its position as a net oil and gas exporter, a growing current account surplus supported by services and electrical and electronics (E&E) exports, as well as a strong investment cycle from both foreign and domestic sources.
NON-TECH SECTOR INTEREST?

In contrast, Kenanga Investment Bank head of research Peter Kong expects the benchmark index to edge higher next week, supported by renewed buying interest in non-technology sectors, particularly banking, utilities and healthcare.

"We expect the KLCI to move mildly higher next week," he said, adding that the research house continued to favour technology companies with stronger revenue visibility, including Kelington Group Bhd, UWC Technology Bhd and Frontken Corporation Bhd.
He said sentiment towards technology stocks remained weak amid valuation concerns, although Kenanga did not anticipate a material impact on corporate earnings in 2027 and 2028.
"Data centre related plays however would provide some support as a modest beneficiary on the back of potential slow-down in new approvals in key data centre states in the US," Kong added.
PROJECTIONS TO REMAIN VOLATILE
Affin Hwang has set the highest year-end FBM KLCI target at 1,730 points, followed by Kenanga and MBSB Research at 1,700 points each.
"At this juncture, we view our end-2026 FBM KLCI target of 1,770 points as an optimistic scenario, with a downward bias toward the 1,700-point level," said MBSB Research.

On monetary policy, both Kenanga and Affin Hwang expect Bank Negara Malaysia to raise the overnight policy rate (OPR) by 25 basis points to three per cent in 2027, with Kenanga expecting the adjustment in the first quarter.

Meanwhile, Affin Hwang expects Brent crude oil prices to average between US$80 and US$85 per barrel in 2026 and 2027, while Kenanga said lower crude oil prices would be a key factor in supporting a re-rating of the consumer sector, although prices are expected to remain volatile.
MBSB Research expects Malaysia's economy to grow by 4.6 per cent in 2027, while market consensus points to 6.6 per cent year-on-year earnings growth for FBM KLCI-listed companies.

Overall, while global uncertainties are expected to keep market sentiment cautious, analysts believe Malaysia's resilient economic outlook and positive corporate earnings prospects could provide some stability to the benchmark index in the weeks ahead.

9db1676e34bca0ee: KUALA LUMPUR: An attempted theft of earthing cables along the MRT Putrajaya Line was foiled after a man was arrested in an intelligence-led operation by Rapid KL auxiliary police.
Rapid KL said the arrest followed an attempted cable theft on Saturday, which disrupted train services on the line.

Following the incident, auxiliary police and the Putrajaya Line operations team stepped up patrols, surveillance and security checks at identified high-risk locations, including during the Deepavali holiday period.
In a patrol at about 1pm on Nov 8, auxiliary police personnel found several earthing cables believed to have been targeted by thieves near an electrical substation (BSS) close to Jinjang station.
"Checks found that the cables had been cut elsewhere before being left at the substation, believed to be awaiting collection and removal," it said in a statement today.
Rapid KL said surveillance and monitoring continued in the surrounding area, including along the stretch between Jinjang and Metro Prima stations, to track down those involved.
At 11.57pm, a lorry was spotted entering the area and was believed to have been used to transport the cut cables.
However, the lorry driver fled during the raid, while auxiliary police personnel arrested a suspect and handed him over to the police for further action and investigation.
Rapid KL said this was the second arrest involving attempted cable theft within its operational areas in a week.

It warned that cable theft and trespassing onto railway tracks were not only criminal offences but could also endanger those involved, damage critical infrastructure and disrupt public transport services.
It said it would continue working with the authorities and strengthen security measures to protect its assets and ensure reliable train services.
73f54ef4d96b92e7: BEIJING: Australian coach John Aloisi has been sacked as coach of Chengdu Rongcheng after his team squandered a huge lead at the top of the table to miss out on the Chinese Super League (CSL) title at the weekend.
Chengdu lost their last four matches to give up a lead which once stood at 12 points, allowing Dalian Yingbo to overhaul them and claim a first CSL title after a 3-1 win over Tianjin Tiger on Sunday.
"Mr. John Aloisi will no longer serve as head coach of Chengdu Rongcheng Football Club, and his staff will leave together," the club said in a statement on its official WeChat account late on Monday.
The former Australia international striker, who took over for this season, was not the only head to roll with the club also announcing that Chairman Wang Lei and General Manager Wu Bo had resigned.
Chengdu Rongcheng were in the Chinese fourth division as recently as 2018 before making their way up the pyramid to reach the top flight in 2022.
They finished fifth, fourth and third twice in their first four seasons and needed only a single point from their last four games to secure a first title this year.

Sunday's 3-2 loss to Shandong Taishan handed Dalian the title on a better head-to-head record after they recorded a pair of wins over Chengdu, including a 1-0 victory in the penultimate round of matches.
f3d19977e3716664: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's building material market saw mixed movements in October, marked by a sharp drop in steel prices alongside moderate upticks in sand and cement, according to the Statistics Department.

Monthly unit price index for sand rose between 0.3 and 1.8 per cent across selected areas, with Sandakan recording the highest monthly increase, followed by Kuching (0.8 per cent) and Johor (0.5 per cent).

Cement price indices also recorded slight month-on-month gains ranging from 0.1 to 0.4 per cent. Perak led the monthly rise, while Terengganu, Kelantan and Kuching each recorded an increase of 0.3 per cent.
Despite these marginal monthly index adjustments, the nationwide average price of ordinary Portland cement remained unchanged in October at RM25.80 per 50 kg bag.
On an annual basis, however, the cement unit price index climbed between 0.6 and 7.4 per cent across most parts of Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah, and Sarawak compared to October 2025.

The strongest year-on-year increases were posted in the combined region of Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Melaka and Negeri Sembilan (7.4 per cent), followed by Terengganu, Kelantan and Kuching at 5.7 per cent each.
In contrast, steel prices extended their downward trajectory.

The average per-unit price of steel—comprising mild steel round bars and Mycon 60 high tensile deformed bars—fell 3.0 per cent month-on-month to RM3,327.30 per metric tonne, down from RM3,431.90 per metric tonne in September.

On a month-on-month basis, the unit price index for steel fell between 0.2 and 10.5 per cent across selected regions, with the highest drop in Perak, followed with a 3.6 per cent decline in Terengganu and Kelantan, and a 1.3 per cent slip in Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Melaka and Negeri Sembilan.

Year-on-year, steel unit price indices retreated between 0.6 and 8.2 per cent across all surveyed areas nationwide, according to the department. Perak posted the largest annual contraction at 8.2 per cent, followed by Terengganu and Kelantan (-4.8 per cent) and Miri (-4.0 per cent).
Reflecting the broader decline in steel costs, the Building Material Cost Index (BCI) with steel bars showed regional variation.

In the peninsular, the monthly BCI with steel bars decreased between 0.1 and 3.8 per cent across building categories and regions, while in Sabah, Sandakan posted minor increases of 0.1 to 0.2 per cent, while Kota Kinabalu's prices were unchanged compared to in September.
In Sarawak, Sibu recorded slight decreases between 0.1 and 0.4 per cent across all categories of buildings, whereas Kuching and Miri registered slight increases between 0.1 per cent and 0.2 per cent.
23d7b6245637e5ff: HONG KONG, Nov 10 — Asian stocks rallied today to extend a Wall Street surge led by technology firms as investors took advantage of lower prices following last week’s rout, while another plunge in oil prices added to the upbeat mood.
AI-linked firms led gains across the region, in stark contrast to the battering in reaction to last Tuesday’s Democratic sweep of Congress that stoked regulatory concerns.

However, traders remain on edge about profitability in light of the vast sums pumped into the sector, while they were also keeping tabs on Nvidia after boss Jensen Huang’s admission of an affair amid speculation of a Chinese espionage plot.

Titans including Amazon, Microsoft and Apple were among the big gainers yesterday in New York as tech bounced back with help from bargain-hunting, with observers pointing out that confidence in the AI outlook remained solid.
The Nasdaq’s 2.7 per cent spike led a strong day on Wall Street, and Asian investors took up the baton.

Seoul surged more than five per cent at one point thanks to similar advances for chipmakers SK hynix and Samsung, while Tokyo jumped almost three per cent on the back of strong performances by Kioxia, SoftBank and Tokyo Electron.
Taiwan’s TSMC rallied more than one per cent and MediaTek more than seven per cent to drag the Taiex 3.5 per cent higher.
Hong Kong, Shanghai, Sydney, Singapore, Manila and Wellington were also higher.
However, SPI Asset Management’s Stephen Innes said the gains did not suggest markets were back in rude health.
“The market rallied because the sellers stepped away, not because the entire buy-side suddenly rediscovered its courage,” he wrote in a commentary.

“For the second consecutive session, the companies receiving the enormous capital expenditure cheques dramatically outperformed the businesses writing them. That is a potentially important development after last week’s indiscriminate liquidation,” he said.
‘Positive momentum’
“The hyperscalers remain central to the AI investment cycle, but the market is increasingly questioning the returns on the extraordinary sums being committed to new infrastructure.

“Equipment providers, optical networking companies and selected data-centre suppliers can still benefit from existing spending programmes, even as investors become more selective about the ultimate economics for the companies funding those projects.”
Oil prices continued their retreat on hopes the US and Iran will eventually bring an end to the Middle East crisis.
Both main contracts fell around one per cent today, extending the previous day’s drop that saw Brent give up almost six per cent.
They have lost around 20 per cent this month as traders bet on a resolution to the seven-month-old conflict, which has sent inflation soaring and forced central banks to hike interest rates.
US President Donald Trump said yesterday there was “positive momentum” toward ending the war after meeting Qatar’s prime minister at the White House.
“I had an excellent conversation with Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani,” Trump said on Truth Social, adding that “much was discussed with respect to the Islamic Republic of Iran”.
While expectations had grown ahead of last week’s midterms that he would resume strikes on Iran this month, Trump has talked down such a move while leaving the door open to them.

In his post yesterday, Trump reiterated that the US was “locked and loaded,” but that he believed further strikes were “quite unlikely” given that key US allies in the Gulf “would prefer the status quo”.
His comments echoed early statements to CNN over the weekend when he said it was “highly unlikely” fighting would resume.

70e13f6adeaadb02: KOTA KINABALU: The Sabah government should adopt a more transparent approach to infrastructure development, particularly in the disclosure of project details and public spending, said an academic.

Universiti Teknologi Sabah senior lecturer Dr Jain Yassin said it was encouraging that the state government continued to prioritise basic infrastructure, particularly water supply and road connectivity.
"These are fundamental necessities that directly affect people's quality of life and the state's economic activities.

"However, beyond the amount of budget allocated for infrastructure, I believe we should pay greater attention to three important aspects: the rate of project completion, the quality and sustainability of infrastructure, and accountability and transparency in public expenditure.
"The Sabah government has to adopt a more transparent approach by publicly disclosing project contractors, contract values, implementation timelines and project progress.

"This should be a shared commitment between the state and federal governments to ensure that public funds are managed responsibly," said Jain, who is also an adviser to the All-Party Parliamentary Group Malaysia-SDG (Sabah region), in an interview with the New Straits Times.
He was commenting on the announcement by Sabah Finance Minister Datuk Seri Masidi Manjun that the state was expected to table a larger budget next year.
Beyond addressing basic infrastructure gaps, Jain said the state should focus on strengthening its economic capacity, diversifying its economy and developing new engines of growth.
He said Sabah should begin investing in new sources of economic growth.
"For instance, in preparation for Visit Sabah 2027, budget allocations should go beyond tourism promotion and attracting visitors.
"We need to prepare local businesses, Small and Medium Enterprises (SME) and communities to participate in the tourism value chain and capture the economic benefits.

"Similarly, with the Blue Economy already identified as an important development agenda, it is time to translate the planning into actual projects, investment and economic activities that create jobs and generate income for local communities."
58ba6cd66c3fc3ab: OXFORD: An Oxford University museum on Monday returned the remains of 39 people taken during Britain's colonial rule in India to members of its Naga community.

Almost 30 people from the community based in northeastern Nagaland, a mountainous state bordering Myanmar, travelled to Britain for the ceremony, which the museum's director, Laura Van Broekhoven, called a "historic moment."

The handover at the Pitt Rivers Museum came as part of a broader trend among Western museums reassessing how they acquired exhibits from other cultures, particularly human remains, and in some cases returning them.
The Pitt Rivers, an ethnographic museum founded in the 19th century, has already handed back human remains to Indigenous communities in Australia, New Zealand and the United States.
The Oxford museum has more than 6,000 objects representing Naga culture, the largest collection in the world, and is giving back "ancestral human remains", mainly skulls, to the Naga people.
Van Broekhoven hailed it as "a historic moment that will be part of stories told to next generations" in a speech as both sides signed a formal agreement on the handover.
The remains were already "on their way to Heathrow" airport, the museum director said, after overcoming "so much red tape everywhere."
The museum only removed all human remains from display in 2020, much later than most museums, and still has around 2,700 remains in storage, she told AFP.
These "were collected in times that had different ethics, different thinking, which was not unproblematic when we look at it with the eyes of today", she said.
- 'RESPECTFUL REST' -
Housed in a Victorian Gothic building, the museum is a dark atmospheric space with glass cases crammed with objects, many with handwritten labels.
Naga tribal leaders united for the handover and planned to bury the remains together under a joint memorial in a park.
"We shall put them to respectful rest," one of the tribal leaders, Thejao Vihienuo, told AFP.
The 73-year-old, draped in a traditional shawl, also visited with other Nagas last year as part of the lengthy process.
"It's been six years of working alongside each other on a very delicate matter," the museum director said.
The Naga remains were brought to Oxford between 1910 and 1940. Most were collected by two colonial administrators who were anthropologists.
The museum says on its website that items collected during this era were "frequently confiscated during punitive military expeditions, rather than freely given."
While in Oxford, the delegation met descendants of one of the anthropologists.
"The manner in which these human remains were taken away from our land leaves much for us to speculate," said Vihienuo.
"I suspect that nobody would have given the skull of his father or his grandfather as a gift to another person."

The Naga people once practiced headhunting, severing heads of enemies as trophies, but also kept heads of their own chiefs "at the centre of the villages" and one of the remains is a chief's head, said anthropologist Dolly Kikon, a member of Nagaland's Lotha-Naga community.--AFP

80dddfe3de96a65f: MELAKA: Pakatan Harapan will discuss its political direction, including the possibility of exploring new cooperation with other parties, only after the Melaka election.

Acting Melaka PKR chairman Adam Adli Abd Halim said any decision on political cooperation must first be discussed by the PH Presidential Council before it could be regarded as the coalition's official position.

"For now, we are focused on concluding our campaign ahead of polling day. We have seen several recent political developments, including the emergence of new political alignments, and we do not deny that.
"I see this as one of the dynamics that we need to observe.

"At the PH level, in particular, decisions of this nature will be discussed thoroughly by the Presidential Council before we can arrive at a resolution that can serve as the coalition's direction," he told a daily PH press conference at the coalition's main operations room here today.

He was commenting on a statement by Bersatu secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali, who had hinted at the possibility of a more open understanding between the party and PH towards the end of the Melaka election campaign, while stressing that Bersatu could not stand alone.
Adam Adli said recent political developments did not necessarily reflect the parties' official positions unless the matters had been discussed and decided by the Presidential Council.
"We know that recent developments have sometimes given an indication of possible moves ahead.
"However, as long as there is no specific decision on the matter and it has not been discussed by the Presidential Council, we cannot regard it as official.

"We acknowledge that PH itself needs to reassess its political direction after this state election, especially with the General Election expected to take place sometime next year. This requires us to formulate appropriate strategies and approaches," he said.
He added that PH's priority at present was to secure victories for its candidates.
"What has been discussed previously goes only as far as that. As polling day approaches, I believe our focus should be on securing victories for PH candidates," he said.
90f34b7437f99d77: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's Industrial Production Index (IPI) expanded 6.3 per cent year-on-year in September, driven primarily by strong manufacturing output that propelled the sector's monthly sales value to RM191.1 billion.

According to the latest figures released by the Statistics Department (DOSM), the September headline growth was underpinned by expansions in manufacturing and electricity generation, which offset continued weakness in mining.
The manufacturing output sector advanced 9.4 per cent year-on-year (August 2026: 7.4 per cent), while electricity generation surged 10.7 per cent (August 2026: 9.0 per cent).

Conversely, the mining sector contracted 9.4 per cent (August 2026: -7.4 per cent), dragged down by lower output in crude petroleum and condensate (-11.8 per cent) as well as natural gas (-7.9 per cent).
On a month-on-month comparison, the IPI rose 1.3 per cent (August 2026: 2.6 per cent), supported by a 2.9 per cent expansion in the manufacturing sector.
The growth momentum in manufacturing production was anchored by export-oriented industries, which expanded 10.7 per cent in September compared to 9.1 per cent in August.

This performance was led by the manufacture of computer, electronic, and optical products, which jumped 19.3 per cent, followed by the manufacture of vegetable and animal oils and fats at 7.9 per cent.

Domestic-oriented industries also gathered pace, rising 6.6 per cent year-on-year (August 2026: 3.9 per cent). Growth was lifted by the 10.6 per cent increase in the manufacture of motor vehicles, trailers, and semi-trailers as well as 10.2 per cent for basic metals.
Meanwhile, processed food products production growth saw an increase of 7.5 per cent in September compared with a year ago.
Reflecting the higher factory activity, the capacity utilisation rate of Malaysia's manufacturing industry climbed to 84.9 per cent in September from 84.1 per cent in August.
High plant usage was bolstered by electrical and electronic products at 88.6 per cent, as well as petroleum, chemical, rubber, and plastic products at 81.7 per cent.

The manufacturing sector's sales value in September surged 12.9 per cent year-on-year to RM191.1 billion, accelerating from a 9.9 per cent expansion (RM185.0 billion) recorded in August. Month-on-month, sales value grew by 3.3 per cent.
The sector engaged 2.45 million employees during the month, representing a 1.4 per cent increase from a year earlier. Total salaries and wages paid climbed 4.0 per cent to RM8.7 billion.
As a result, sales value per employee grew 11.3 per cent to RM78,082, while average monthly salaries per employee rose 2.6 per cent to RM3,568.
For the third quarter of 2026 (Q3 2026), the IPI maintained a solid trajectory, advancing 5.3 per cent year-on-year (Q2 2026: 7.7 per cent) and expanding 4.3 per cent quarter-on-quarter.
Growth during the quarter was anchored by manufacturing (7.8 per cent) and electricity (8.3 per cent), which cushioned a 6.7 per cent contraction in mining.
Manufacturing sales value for Q3 2026 grew 10.7 per cent year-on-year to RM553.5 billion (Q2 2026: 9.3 per cent; RM524.8 billion), logging a 5.5 per cent quarter-on-quarter increase.
The sector's quarterly wage bill stood at RM25.8 billion—up 3.4 per cent—with sales value per employee rising 9.1 per cent to RM226,091 and average monthly salaries advancing 2.0 per cent to RM3,517.

Cumulatively, for the first nine months ended September 2026, Malaysia's overall IPI registered a growth of 5.7 per cent, significantly outpacing the 2.9 per cent growth recorded in the corresponding period of 2025.

Over the same nine-month period, manufacturing sales value reached RM1.58 trillion, up 8.5 per cent compared to 3.6 per cent growth in January–September 2025, while total salaries and wages paid reached RM77.4 billion, reflecting an increase of 2.9 per cent.

213814222963ae16: PARIS, Nov 10 — France defender Ibrahima Konate said yesterday that Kylian Mbappe was in a good place as he returns to national team action despite missing out on the Ballon d’Or and the controversy in China sparked by his comments about Mao Zedong.
Mbappe, who missed Les Bleus’ last three matches through injury, has returned to coach Zinedine Zidane’s squad ahead of their Nations League matches with Italy and Turkey this week.
“He’s in a very good frame of mind; you can see that from his recent matches — he’s been decisive. He’s absolutely vital for us in Madrid,” Konate, who also plays with Mbappe at Real Madrid, said.

Mbappe narrowly lost out on the Ballon d’Or to England and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane in late October and then had to apologise after a social media storm following a video in which he joked about former Chinese leader Mao.

In a clip from an interview with French show “The Bridge”, which has since been taken down, Mbappe had said he was amused by an internet meme showing his face photoshopped onto “some guy, think he’s a Chinese dictator”, an apparent reference to Mao.
Major Chinese brands subsequently cut ties with the 27-year-old, and Spanish La Liga matches have been pulled from state television broadcaster CCTV.
Konate added that the 2018 World Cup winner had also put any Ballon d’Or disappointment firmly behind him.

“He’s a competitor, so of course not winning the Ballon d’Or when he thoroughly deserved it is tough, but the very next day he was giving it his all in training. I hope he’ll be in top form next year to lift it,” the former Liverpool centre-half said. — AFP

e2d481ef5903fc20: KULAI, Nov 10 — The DAP wants to continue playing its role as a nation-building party, regardless of whether it is in government or the opposition, by championing transparent, fair and sustainable policies, said its vice-president Teo Nie Ching.

Teo, who is also deputy communications minister, said the principle formed the basis of DAP’s struggle to ensure Malaysia continued to develop as a nation with a sustainable governance system, while prioritising the interests and welfare of the people.
“Regardless of whether we are in the opposition or in government, we want to be a nation builder.
“… we want to develop our country together, and that is why we want to ensure that we can make Malaysia a country with a sustainable system,” she said in an exclusive interview with Bernama recently.

The Wanita DAP chief said the party’s contribution to nation-building was not confined to economic and physical development, but also included efforts to strengthen inclusive and fair policies, including taking into account the needs of women and children.

Commenting on DAP’s participation in the Madani Government, Teo said its position provided the party with an opportunity to translate its principles into policies and action through direct involvement in the country’s administration.
The Kulai MP said the priority was to ensure that the policies it championed could be implemented transparently and benefit the people, thereby contributing to the country’s long-term development.
“Our intention is to ensure that we can contribute to nation-building by ensuring that we have policies that are more open and transparent,” she said.

Asked about DAP’s approach ahead of the 16th General Election, Teo said the party left it to the people to make their own assessment, but efforts to win over voters should be based on its achievements and track record during its time in government.

She cited the establishment of the Malaysian Media Council (MMM), which was among the reform agendas championed by the party for more than 50 years before being realised through the passage of the Malaysian Media Council Act under the Madani Government.
“Malaysia now has the MMM, chaired by a former Federal Court judge, demonstrating the efforts to realise the institutional reform agenda under the Madani Government.

“In addition, Pakatan Harapan has also championed the proposal to limit the Prime Minister’s term of office, with Penang becoming the first state to amend its state constitution to limit the Chief Minister’s tenure to 10 years. The agenda was subsequently brought to the federal government level, with the hope that the proposal would be passed in the Dewan Rakyat,” she said.

Touching on the challenges of implementing policies while in government, Teo said not all decisions received the support of every party, particularly when the interests of certain groups were involved.
She said this was among the challenges faced by parties in government, but their track record in implementing policies should serve as evidence to the people of the efforts undertaken.
“I believe that being in government does come with its pros and cons. The cons are quite obvious because not all policies will be supported by everyone.

bedce5a870a66313: LOS ANGELES, Nov 10 — Aryna Sabalenka battled past Karolina Muchova in straight sets to make a winning start at the season-ending WTA Finals in Indian Wells yesterday.
Former world number one Sabalenka was forced to dig deep before finally prevailing 7-6 (7/2), 7-5 in just under two hours.
Second-seeded Sabalenka is chasing her first ever WTA Finals victory after suffering defeats in the 2022 and 2025 finals.
The four-time Grand Slam champion from Belarus looked to be in trouble after conceding a break of serve to go 5-4 down in the opening set.
But Sabalenka broke back immediately for 5-5 and subsequently went on to hold her nerve in the tie-break 7-2 to seize the early initiative.
Both players struggled on serve in the second set, with Sabalenka suffering her fourth break as she served for the match at 5-4 up.

Crucially though Sabalenka responded to that stumble by breaking back immediately to lead 6-5 and she made no mistake when serving for the match again, wrapping up victory when Czech opponent Muchova netted a backhand.
Sabalenka and Muchova’s group two duel was the first of two matches on Monday, with third seed Mirra Andreeva facing Elina Svitolina later in the day.
This year’s WTA Finals were scheduled to be held in Saudi Arabia but in July were moved to Indian Wells after US military strikes on Iran in February and the subsequent war in the region. — AFP

383746de14e71744: BUKIT MERTAJAM: Three Myanmar children pleaded not guilty at the magistrate's court today to a charge of criminally intimidating an elderly woman.

The three — comprising two 11-year-olds and a 12-year-old — maintained their innocence after the joint charge was read to them in Myanmar by a court-appointed Myanmar interpreter before magistrate Roshayati Radellah.
They were accused of threatening to cause injury to a 71-year-old woman using various objects, including a mop, an iron rod, a fluorescent tube, and stones.
The offence allegedly occurred outside a house in Tingkat Binjai Empat Belas, Taman Sri Rambai about 6pm on Oct 22.
The charge was framed under Section 506 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34, which provides for up to two years' imprisonment, a fine, or both upon conviction.

During proceedings, their counsel S. Sagthiyaraj, who is representing them pro bono under the Penang Legal Aid Centre, confirmed receiving the relevant documents from Deputy Public Prosecutor Zulfadzli Hassan.
He requested a date for case management, and the magistrate fixed Dec 18.
The three children previously claimed trial to the same charge on Oct 30 when it was read to them in Bahasa Malaysia.
The court had then fixed today's hearing for a Myanmar interpreter to be appointed to explain the charge to them. Bail was initially denied.
However, speaking to reporters after today's proceedings, Sagthiyaraj said all three children had since been released on RM4,000 bail each following an urgent revision at the High Court.
He said the judicial revision was initiated by the magistrate on Oct 30 after procedural irregularities involving Section 84 of the Child Act 2001 were identified.
The provision stipulates that children charged with non-capital offences cannot be detained on remand and must be released on bail into the custody of their parents or guardians.

Sagthiyaraj said the children, who attend an NGO-run school, had initially struggled to understand the court proceedings due to language barriers and were briefly sent to a moral rehabilitation centre in Air Itam.

"Following swift interventions and concerns raised by non-governmental organisations, the learned magistrate filed an urgent revision before Judicial Commissioner Suraiya Mustafa Kamal at the Butterworth High Court.
"The emergency hearing took place at 5.45pm and concluded at 6.45pm that same day, with the same Deputy Public Prosecutor handling the matter.
"The High Court allowed bail at RM4,000 for each child, with their respective parents acting as sole sureties," he said.
Sagthiyaraj said the children were subsequently brought back to the Bukit Mertajam court complex to complete the necessary documentation and were released at 7.45pm that evening.
e0fb72f404cf7bbd: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said it was too early to discuss a Cabinet reshuffle amid speculation over possible changes to the line-up following Transport Minister Anthony Loke’s decision to resign.

a22ff3abf235e234: TELEKOM Malaysia (TM) is expanding its capabilities in artificial intelligence (AI), cloud computing, cybersecurity and digital infrastructure as it seeks to translate its technological strengths into stronger business growth.
TM's success in securing awards across four categories at the PIKOM Digital Excellence Awards 2026 reflects its ongoing transformation and growing focus on digital services.
A key part of this transformation has been the application of technology to improve its own operations.
At the core of TM's strategy is a scalable, end-to-end digital ecosystem designed to reduce operational friction and accelerate growth for consumers and businesses.

TM has significantly transformed its Digital Business Support System, streamlining its product portfolio by more than 99 per cent and reducing launch times from months to just three weeks, while maintaining operational stability.

This agile foundation strengthens TM's ability to respond to customer needs more quickly, introduce new services efficiently and deliver integrated Quad Play solutions spanning fixed voice and broadband, mobile and lifestyle services.
The same approach applies to AI
Rather than treating AI as a standalone technology trend, TM has focused on applications that improve customer experience, automate processes and support better decision-making.
Combined with its cloud, data and cybersecurity capabilities, this approach enables AI to be deployed within a secure and well-governed environment.
TM's strength lies in its ability to integrate a broad range of capabilities, from connectivity and cloud computing to cybersecurity, AI and digital platforms.
These capabilities increasingly work together to address customer needs, while partnerships enable the group to draw on additional expertise and solutions where they add value.
This reflects TM's ambition to evolve from a traditional connectivity provider into an orchestrator of a broader digital ecosystem.
Sustainability is also becoming an integral part of this transformation

In 2025, TM's data centre ecosystem avoided more than 190,000MWh of energy consumption and over 149,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2e) in annual emissions through load optimisation and resource sharing.
The group is also applying technology to initiatives such as smart urban forestry and helping micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) adopt practical digital tools.

As Malaysia strengthens its position as a regional digital hub, the challenge is increasingly about translating infrastructure investment into stronger local businesses, deeper digital capabilities, a skilled workforce and long-term economic value.

For TM, the next phase of growth will depend on converting its infrastructure and technological capabilities into greater commercial value, while helping Malaysian businesses and the country capture more opportunities from the digital economy.

e29f19a4b4f0e925: KUALA LUMPUR: Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) could tap new opportunities in the domestic natural gas market as Malaysia's growing data centre industry drives demand for electricity, said Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani.
He said the rising electricity requirements of data centres could create another commercially attractive market for natural gas, provided it is supplied at market prices without subsidies.

"In the past, Petronas signed long-term contracts with countries such as Japan to export gas. However, with the growth of data centres, there is an opportunity to supply gas for power generation and sell electricity at retail prices.
"Under long-term export agreements, gas is sold at wholesale prices. But by supplying power to data centres, there is an opportunity to obtain commercial market prices.

"Petronas can embark on this, and still export, sell to the data centres. And data centres will pay you the price," he said in his keynote address at the Bursa Malaysia Sectoral Series: Powering the AI Era.

Johari said the growing electricity demand from data centres could also create opportunities to expand and diversify Malaysia's energy supply, particularly through the integration of solar power with battery energy storage systems (BESS).
He said BESS could play a complementary role in the country's energy distribution system by improving efficiency and managing fluctuations in electricity supply.
"For example, batteries can store electricity when generation exceeds immediate demand and release it when needed," he said.

Johari said meeting the rising demand for electricity presents both challenges and opportunities, particularly in attracting new investments in power generation, energy storage, grid technologies, engineering and domestic supply chains.
He said priority should be given to mobilising capital towards solutions that can support Malaysia's long-term energy requirements.
"Ultimately, Malaysia's ambition is not merely to attract more data-centre investments, but to build the infrastructure necessary for a competitive digital economy.

"This must be achieved without compromising the reliability and affordability of electricity for households and existing industries, or the sustainable management of the country's natural resources," he added.

ee988588affb19ba: RIYADH, Nov 10 — Saudi Arabia’s East-West oil pipeline, essential for bypassing the Strait of Hormuz, was attacked yesterday but operations were unaffected, official media said, as the kingdom and Yemen’s Houthis traded strikes.

“No injuries or fatalities were reported, and pipeline operations were unaffected,” the report said.
The report did not say who was responsible, but Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis have repeatedly targeted Saudi oil infrastructure with drones and missiles.

The East-West pipeline, which enables the world’s largest crude exporter to get its oil to market via the Red Sea, has taken on increased significance during the Middle East war as Iran seeks to choke off the main route for Gulf energy shipments through the Strait of Hormuz.
Earlier yesterday, Saudi authorities warned Riyadh residents of “a hostile aerial threat”, a day after an attack on a skyscraper belonging to oil giant Aramco rattled the capital’s business district.
“Please remain calm, stay indoors or in a safe place away from windows and doors, and follow the instructions of Civil Defence,” the alert said, before the warning was lifted minutes later.
Saudi Arabia has faced near-daily strikes from the Houthis for weeks after a truce in their long-running conflict unravelled in July.
Yesterday evening, parents of students were alerted that schools in Riyadh were returning to online classes “as part of the ongoing precautionary measures”.

Students had only been back in the classroom for two days following weeks of distance learning, and the message to parents, which was seen by AFP, did not say how long the new interval was expected to last.
The Houthis, who control large parts of Yemen, Saudi Arabia’s impoverished southern neighbour, did not announce a fresh attack on Riyadh yesterday.
But they did report a Saudi strike on Hodeida airport on the Red Sea, which has long been out of use.
The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said yesterday that it had destroyed three facilities producing missile parts and fuel, without specifying where.
The Houthis’ Almasirah television also said the death toll from weekend Saudi strikes on a village in Sanaa province had climbed to 44, including more than 20 children.
On Sunday, the Houthis claimed attacks on Riyadh’s business district, where witnesses said Aramco Tower was damaged.
Saudi authorities said the building suffered minor damage from falling shrapnel after an “attempted attack”.
The Houthis have repeatedly targeted Aramco tankers, refineries, storage areas and the company’s headquarters.

The Saudi-led coalition initially launched hostilities with the Houthis in March 2015, months after the group seized the capital Sanaa, forcing out Yemen’s internationally recognised government. — AFP

National coach Brendon Carolan had said a few youngsters may be included for the Sultan Azlan Shah Cup.

"To date I have not received a call-up for national training, but I am keeping my fingers crossed that it will come by next year," said Naaveennash who turns out for Tenaga Nasional in the ongoing Malaysia Hockey League (MHL) where he has scored three goals so far.

943bd3c8c162b580: SEMPORNA: Three people, including two Chinese tourists, were injured after their tourist boat suffered engine trouble and was rammed by another vessel near Pulau Singamata yesterday.
The incident occurred at 11.12am as the boat, carrying eight Chinese tourists, a skipper and three crew members, was travelling from Seafest Jetty to Pulau Bohey Dulang.
Semporna police chief Superintendent Tan Hiap Wah said the boat had stopped in the waters off Pulau Singamata after its engine became entangled in debris.
He said the vessel was struck from behind by another tourist boat while its crew were trying to remove the debris.
"The collision left two Chinese tourists, a 29-year-old man and a 28-year-old woman, as well as one crew member of the first boat with minor injuries," he said in a statement today.
The first boat sustained damage to its rear section, while the skipper and a crew member of the second boat escaped unhurt. Their vessel was also undamaged.
Tan said police received a report from a 39-year-old local man who worked as a boat operator for a tourism company.

The case is being investigated under Section 280 of the Penal Code for negligent navigation of a vessel and Section 337 for causing hurt through an act endangering the life or personal safety of others.
df8d5aa126bb1f6a: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said it was too early to discuss the possibility of a cabinet reshuffle.
This follows speculation over the positions of Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan and Transport Minister Anthony Loke, amid the possibility of two vacancies in the cabinet.
Amir Hamzah's term as a Dewan Negara member expires next month. His appointment would need to be extended for him to remain in the cabinet.

Loke, meanwhile, is expected to resign, with his resignation to take effect once former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak arrives at his residence to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest.
"It's too early," Anwar said when asked about a cabinet reshuffle.
He was speaking after officiating the International Construction Week and International Building and Construction Exhibition.
Asked about Amir Hamzah's position, Anwar said: "Is that so? He has yet to say so."
Earlier, Utusan Malaysia reported that the unity government was expected to undertake a minor cabinet reshuffle following the possibility of two vacancies.
The report, citing sources, said the developments involved Loke and Amir Hamzah.
97a341dab0d8388a: NEW YORK, Nov 10 — Boeing will cut about five per cent of its commercial plane workforce as it moderates the pace of ramping up jet production, the company said yesterday.

The company will eliminate the posts through a mix of layoffs and attrition because of a slower ramp-up to “provide our factories and supply chain partners additional time to achieve stability,” said a message to employees from Boeing commercial chief Stephanie Pope.
“Adjusting our production schedules and reducing aircraft output puts us in an overstaffed position,” she added.
Pope praised the team for improved operations reflected in US certifications this year of the 737 MAX 7 and 737 MAX 10.

“While we have made substantial progress, we have not yet fully recovered,” said Pope, who promised to treat employees with “dignity and respect” as the company moves ahead with layoff notifications beginning in December.

Boeing executives had previously signalled slower plans to raise plane output, saying in a late October conference call the company would no longer meet its target for 2026 deliveries and that it had pushed back the timeframe for lifting 737 MAX production to 52 from 47 until the second half of 2027.

Raising 737 MAX output has been viewed by investors as central to revenue and profit growth after a long period of financial losses due to safety problems, including two deadly MAX crashes in 2018 and 2019.
“We’re making progress, but we still have more work to do, and I’m expecting it’ll take us into next year to get fully stable at this rate,” CEO Kelly Ortberg said October 27.
Ortberg cited the need for greater predictability in wing production and with the production of fuselages at its Kansas operation.
Shares of Boeing were down less than 0.1 per cent after midday. — AFP
15f1e35039cb8904: KUANTAN: Floods are forecast to hit Rompin and Jerantut from 1am tomorrow until 11.59pm on Nov 14, according to the National Flood Forecasting and Warning Centre of the Department of Irrigation and Drainage.
In a statement, the centre said flooding could occur in areas along the Rompin and Pahang river basins, particularly low-lying and flood-prone locations.

"Other areas include low-lying locations within a 5km radius of the Pahang River Basin, covering Kampung Mikang, Kampung Buluh Nipis, Kampung Simpang Sepayang, Kampung Sepayang, Kampung Tebu Hitam, Kampung Tengah, Kampung Tekek, Perumahan Murah Kampung Tekek, Kampung Serinkin, and Kampung Janglau 1, 2 and 3," it said.

In Jerantut, areas at risk include low-lying locations within a 5km radius of the Pahang River Basin, covering Perumahan Felda Jengka 24 in Block 11, Taman Ria, Perumahan Sungai Jan and Felda Gelanggi 1 and 3.

6d4a0dc2e8a52142: PETALING JAYA: Former Penang chief minister Lim Guan Eng has rejected preacher Firdaus Wong's defamation claim, arguing that his remarks about the preacher were made in response to Wong's own provocative social media comments.

In a response to Wong's letter of demand, Lim's lawyers said the DAP adviser's June 24 Facebook video had been taken out of context and that Wong had selectively quoted and inaccurately translated portions of the Mandarin-language recording.
The dispute reportedly began after Lim published a Facebook post on June 15 promoting an annual pork-selling event in Butterworth in conjunction with the Dragon Boat Festival.
Wong mocked the post, allegedly suggesting that DAP establish a non-Muslim religious affairs bureau and making sarcastic remarks about the party organising a pork-selling programme.
In the defence filed by legal firm Guok Partnership last week, Lim's lawyers said their client was entitled to respond to Wong's comments, which they viewed as having racial and religious overtones.
They maintained that Lim's video should be considered in its entirety rather than through isolated extracts, arguing that Wong had misrepresented its intended meaning.
Lim denies defaming Wong and has rejected his demands for an open apology and RM5 million in damages.
His legal team has indicated that it will rely on the defences of justification, fair comment and qualified privilege should the matter proceed to trial.

Wong filed a defamation suit against Lim at the Penang High Court, claiming the former chief minister portrayed him as an intolerant religious extremist seeking to undermine the freedoms and rights of non-Muslims.
In his statement of claim, Wong alleged that the remarks were malicious and intended to incite hatred against him among the non-Muslim community.
He is seeking general, aggravated and exemplary damages, as well as an injunction against Lim.
858ba641b68502cf: Cisco will no longer create products that don’t integrate with Cloud Control, its SaaS-y management platform that offers netadmins a single tool to manage all of the networking giant’s devices and much of its software portfolio.

The networking giant announced Cloud Control in June 2025 and only made it available to customers in the USA. Cisco has previously told The Register that slow rollout reflects the fact that Cisco needs to nail privacy and other regulatory niceties, and deploy infrastructure, before introducing the service to other markets.

It appears Cisco is now satisfied it has sorted out those issues. Jeff Schultz, Cisco’s senior vice president for portfolio strategy and marketing, today told the company’s Live conference in Australia that Cloud Control will come online in the European Union, UK, and Down Under in February 2027. Japan, India, and Canada will get their turn in May.
Schultz said Cisco is “working tirelessly” to deploy Cloud Control across the world as soon as possible.
He also revealed that, starting next year, Cisco will no longer ship products that don’t integrate with Cloud Control.

That doesn’t mean those products will be manageable only if they can connect to Cloud Control. Instead, the decision reflects Cisco’s belief that the main thing stopping its customers buying more of its products is the complexity of operating them in concert. Schultz also feels that Cloud Control represents “platform advantage” for Cisco, because when users integrate networking, security, and observability the result is better manageability and resilience.

Schultz also told the conference that Cisco will bundle its Thousand Eyes observability and security tool with the “Essentials” and “Advantage” licenses. “We admit it was hard to license and deploy,” he said during his keynote speech, adding that the tool will be deployed automatically with Wi‑Fi 6E and Wi‑Fi 7 hardware.

Another product Cisco plans to bring to more customers is Live Protect, a tool that implements compensating controls for flaws that organizations can’t immediately patch. Live Protect currently works on some switches, plus SD-WAN and WLAN controllers. From December, Cisco will extend it to 8000 series routers, secure firewalls, campus gateway, and to Cloud Control itself. From May 2027, Live Protect will work with Cisco’s ASR 9000 series service aggregation routers and Network Convergence System. ®
582f0d6f1c01f24c: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — Foreign institutions extended their net buying streak to two consecutive weeks on Bursa Malaysia, recording net inflows of US$381.3 million (RM1.54 billion), according to MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB IB).

In its weekly fund flow report for the week ended Nov 6, MBSB IB said foreign institutions were net buyers on all five trading days, with the highest inflow recorded on Tuesday at RM152.4 million, followed by Monday (RM102.5 million), Thursday (RM55.0 million), Friday (RM40.6 million) and Wednesday (RM30.8 million).

“The top three sectors with net inflows from foreign institutions were financial services (RM249.5 million), transportation and logistics (RM199.8 million), and construction (RM191.4 million),” it said.

Meanwhile, the investment bank said the top three sectors recording net foreign outflows were technology (RM221.5 million), plantation (RM126.7 million) and industrial products and services (RM59.8 million).

On the domestic front, local institutions extended their net selling streak to two consecutive weeks, recording net outflows of RM621.0 million, while retail investors continued their net buying streak for the 11th consecutive week, with net inflows amounting to RM239.7 million, it said.

MBSB IB also said average daily trading volume increased across all investor categories, with retail investors up 5.6 per cent, local institutions up 17.6 per cent, and foreign institutions up 16.8 per cent.
At the regional level, foreign investors extended their net selling streak across eight Asian markets to six consecutive weeks, with total net outflows amounting to US$19.54 billion, it said.
The net selling was led by Taiwan, South Korea, Thailand, Vietnam and Indonesia, while India, Malaysia and the Philippines recorded net inflows, it added. — Bernama
0fee566d13e1d14b: MELAKA, Nov 10 — Melaka police have received 19 reports involving various offences, including mischief, mischief by fire and fighting, since campaigning for the 16th Melaka state election began on October 31.
Its chief Datuk Dzulkhairi Mukhtar said 18 investigation papers had been opened over the 11-day period, but no arrests had been made so far.
“Most of the cases are being investigated under Section 427 of the Penal Code for mischief and Section 435 for mischief by fire, particularly incidents involving the burning of flags.

“There have also been cases of incitement and intimidation,” he told reporters after casting his ballot in early voting at the multipurpose hall of the Melaka Police Contingent headquarters in Bukit Beruang here today.
He said campaigning had been peaceful and orderly so far, with no untoward incidents reported.
Dzulkhairi said 669 police personnel had been deployed across the state to monitor election campaigning and maintain public safety and order.
On preparations for polling day this Saturday, he said 3,332 police personnel would be deployed, including officers assigned to monitor the voting process at polling centres throughout the state.
He said the Cantas team would also be deployed on polling day, warning that police would not hesitate to make arrests if any disturbances occurred.
He also urged political party supporters to behave responsibly, abide by the law and refrain from intimidating or coercing voters.
For the latest news on the 16th Melaka state election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/. — Bernama
3188493d3ae00f89: SINGAPORE: Singapore has launched a gold vaulting service for overseas central banks and official institutions, seeking to capitalise on global demand to diversify storage of bullion reserves.

Gold will be stored in the city-state’s national currency vault, which has capacity for as much as 500 tonnes, with room to expand as demand grows, the Monetary Authority of Singapore said in a statement on Tuesday.

“Singapore does not aim to replace other gold centres and gold vaulting services,” MAS chairman Gan Kim Yong, who is also the country’s deputy prime minister, told reporters. “With the growing demand for gold as a reserve asset, I think central banks are also looking for alternatives, looking for more options to strengthen their resilience in terms of their gold reserves,” he said.
MAS will also offer gold custody accounts to select Singapore-based bullion banks with expertise in providing the services, the central bank said in the statement.

The latest push by Singapore comes amid heightened demand for gold from both institutional investors and central banks, which have accumulated the metal at a rapid pace in recent years as geopolitical tensions and concerns over government debt boost its appeal as a haven and a way to diversify investment portfolios.
9c77a38a6ec1be16: BRUSSELS: Prince Harry and his wife Meghan will visit Brussels on Tuesday, a trip that comes days after her estranged father was charged over alleged possession of child sexual abuse images.
The couple, also known as the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, will attend an event at the European Parliament about the dangers facing children on social media.
It will be the first time Meghan has been seen in public since her father Thomas Markle was arrested in Florida on Friday and charged with one count of "possession of child pornography".
It will also mark the first time the couple appear together at a public event abroad since they returned to live in Britain this summer after six years in the United States.
They will open The Lost Screen Memorial displaying images of children affected by online abuse and exploitation.
They had been due to give a joint speech, but only Harry is now expected to speak. He will also take part in a panel event with international activists.
An unnamed source told the UK's Daily Telegraph newspaper that Meghan is "just not strong enough emotionally to be doing any public speaking" following her father's arrest.
An anonymous friend was quoted as saying in the Times that Harry will speak about "child safety".
"You can read into his speech what you will, and it can be taken in any number of ways," they said.
The 82-year-old Markle was taken into custody by FBI agents early Friday at the retirement home where he lives in Lakeland, Florida.

The US Justice Department said Markle allegedly "kept child sexual abuse material (CSAM), including sexually explicit photographs of himself with prepubescent girls, in two Los Angeles-area storage units he rented for nearly two decades."
Markle could face up to 20 years in prison if convicted.
British tabloids reported last month that pictures of child sex abuse had been found at Markle's former home in the Philippines, allegations later confirmed by police in the Southeast Asian country.
He denied those allegations.

Meghan released a statement saying she was "deeply distressed" by the accusations, adding she had blocked contact between him and her children Archie 7, and Lilibet, 5, over previous "troubling and disturbing" allegations.
'Call to action'

Tuesday's event, hosted by Spanish MEP Antonio Lopez-Isturiz, highlights the "urgent need to make the digital world safer for every child", a statement said, adding it was a "call to action" for policymakers, technology companies and society to do more to protect children.
The installation shows 50 enlarged images of children who died as a result of harm they suffered on social media, taken from their parents' lock screens.
Harry and Meghan quit royal duties in early 2020, but carry out similar activities in a private capacity.

On Sunday, Harry attended a Remembrance Day event in a small town, while his father King Charles III led the nation in a two-minute silence at the Cenotaph in London honouring soldiers killed in the line of duty.
66a64da587120c06: IPOH: Police are investigating a fireworks display at a traffic junction along Jalan Kuala Kangsar after a video of the incident went viral on Threads.
The video shows a group of people setting off fireworks at a traffic light-controlled T-junction, while vehicles pass through the area.
Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said police had yet to receive any reports on the incident.
However, he said police would investigate the incident to identify those involved and establish the circumstances surrounding it.
"We will also check whether there are any closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras in the surrounding area that could assist in our investigation.
"Police view this matter seriously as such activities could endanger other road users and should not have happened," he told reporters at the Perak Police Contingent Headquarters.
He said celebrations should be held at appropriate venues without disrupting traffic or inconveniencing the public.
"Celebrations should not be carried out in a manner that affects other road users or the general public," he said.
On the legal provisions that could be invoked, Alwi said police had yet to determine the relevant sections.
"We will conduct a thorough investigation first before deciding which section of the law will be applied," he said.
076b24d97c803fa7: IPOH, Nov 10 — A S$4,000 (RM12,685) job to deliver a package landed a 29-year-old Singaporean in trouble after police found RM1.5 million worth of dried cannabis leaves in his luggage at the Sultan Azlan Shah Airport here on Sunday.

Perak police chief Commissioner Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the suspect had been tricked by a syndicate into believing he was transporting a package containing counterfeit luxury-branded goods.

“Preliminary investigations found that the suspect had come across a job offer through a website promising lucrative payment to transport luggage allegedly containing counterfeit luxury-branded goods to London, England,” he told a press conference at the Perak Police Headquarters here.
He said that the syndicate was believed to have targeted less busy airports, concealing drugs in passengers’ luggage to avoid detection by the authorities.
“If the luggage passes through Customs at these airports, the items will then be sent as cargo and eventually reach their intended destination,” he said.

Mohd Alwi said the suspect was arrested after auxiliary police personnel at the airport detected a suspicious piece of luggage during a baggage inspection at the check-in counter at about 6.20am on November 8.
He said the suspect was scheduled to fly from Ipoh to Singapore, where he would transit before continuing to London.
“Further inspection of the Caggioni-branded zippered suitcase found 36 transparent plastic packets containing dried leaves suspected to be cannabis flower.
“The drugs weighed approximately 19,040 grammes and had an estimated street value of RM1,523,200,” he said.
Mohd Alwi said the amount of drugs seized could have been used by about 47,900 addicts.
He said the suspect and the seized items were subsequently handed over to the Perak Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) for further investigation.
“A preliminary urine screening found that the suspect tested negative for drugs, while checks also found that he had no previous criminal record,” he said.
He also added that the suspect, who is currently unemployed, had been remanded for seven days since November 8.
Mohd Alwi said the case was being investigated under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
“If convicted, the offence carries the death penalty or life imprisonment and whipping of not less than 12 strokes,” he said.
He said the seizure was the result of continuous intelligence-gathering efforts by the NCID, with cooperation from members of the public.
“We will not compromise with any party involved in drug trafficking.
“Possessing, distributing or protecting drug-related activities is a serious offence under the law,” he said.
f2725ae37faab5e4: PETALING JAYA: Empat lagi mangsa kejadian kepala air di Sungai Pertak, Kuala Kubu Bharu, ditemui lemas pagi ini, menjadikan lima mangsa dikesan setakat ini.

"Semua mangsa kini dalam usaha dikeluarkan anggota pasukan mencari dan menyelamat (SAR)," katanya menurut Sinar Harian.
Terdahulu, seorang lelaki tempatan dikenali V Vijayan, 36, ditemui lemas di kawasan Jambatan Pertak pada 1.30 pagi tadi.

Terdahulu, kawasan pencarian dibahagikan kepada empat sektor, iaitu Sektor A dari Lata Jebus ke Lubuk Pertak, Sektor B dari Lubuk Pertak ke Jambatan Dam, Sektor C membabitkan kawasan Jambatan Dam dan Sektor D di kawasan empangan.

Lapan individu dilaporkan dihanyutkan arus dalam kejadian kepala air di beberapa lokasi sekitar Sungai Pertak petang semalam. Mereka terdiri daripada empat warga India dan masing-masing seorang warga Yaman, warga Nepal, warga Sri Lanka serta lelaki tempatan.
Selain dihanyutkan arus, beberapa kumpulan pengunjung dilaporkan terkandas di kawasan Lata Jebus, Kem Sungai Luit dan Gunung Rajah.

cf8c04cdcf6fc894: BEIJING: China's trade surplus surged past US$1 trillion in the first 10 months as a global race to build AI infrastructure buoyed sales of high-tech products and helped offset weak domestic demand, a dynamic likely to sharpen tensions with major trading partners.

The figures highlight Beijing's growing reliance on overseas demand to support an economy hobbled by subdued consumption and a protracted property slump. But while the global AI investment boom is expected to keep demand for Chinese technology products strong into 2027, it risks deepening domestic imbalances and fuelling trade frictions with partners including the EU.

Exports rose sharply by 35.2% in October from the same month last year in US dollar terms, customs data showed on Tuesday, only a touch slower than the 36.3% surge in September, but ahead of economists' forecast for an increase of 33.5%.
That helped lift China's trade surplus to US$1.04 trillion in the first 10 months, topping US$1 trillion for a second consecutive year and reaching the milestone a month earlier than in 2025.

The swelling surplus could fuel further tensions with the European Union, where leaders have called for more trade curbs with China after reaching an agreement with Beijing to limit Chinese exports of hybrid vehicles to the bloc over the next few years. Because the measures have yet to take effect, factories are expected to bring forward shipments, bolstering exports in the near term.

China on Monday officially announced the extension of a trade truce with Washington due to expire on Nov 10 by two months, but said last week that expanding its purchases of US farm goods would hinge on the implementation of their agreed reciprocal tariff-reduction arrangement.

"The risk of additional tariffs and other trade barriers will remain elevated in 2027, particularly as Chinese manufacturers continue expanding their presence in overseas markets," said Joe Peissel, lead macroeconomist at Trivium China.
Imports grew 41.6%, beating the median forecast for a 32% increase in the Reuters poll and accelerating from the 31% growth in September.

The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit will take place next week in the southern Chinese tech and innovation hub Shenzhen, where Chinese president Xi Jinping and US president Donald Trump are expected to meet for the third time so far this year.
One big worry for Beijing is that consumers remain reluctant to spend, constrained by a property market downturn that has battered household wealth and dented confidence in the economic outlook.

Sluggish demand at home has pushed Chinese automakers to seek sales in overseas markets. China's car exports maintained a solid pace of growth in October, while domestic vehicle sales recorded a 12th straight month of declines, separate data released by an industry association showed.
Greater reliance on exports, however, leaves China's economy increasingly exposed to any slowdown in global demand.
Much of the strength in exports this year has been fuelled by a global push to expand AI infrastructure.

"The outlook for exports depends on how long the AI boom will last," Macquarie analysts wrote. They expect China's exports to accelerate further in the fourth quarter before starting to slow from the first quarter of 2027.

04a13e69868fb0c5: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — The ringgit opened marginally higher against the US dollar today amid cautious market sentiment as investors continued to assess global economic developments and the outlook for US interest rates.

fae9af7227d96d4e: BEIJING: China's trade surplus surged past US$1 trillion in the first 10 months as a global race to build AI infrastructure buoyed sales of high-tech products and helped offset weak domestic demand, a dynamic likely to sharpen tensions with major trading partners.
The figures highlight Beijing's growing reliance on overseas demand to support an economy hobbled by subdued consumption and a protracted property slump.

But while the global AI investment boom is expected to keep demand for Chinese technology products strong into 2027, it risks deepening domestic imbalances and fuelling trade frictions with partners, including the European Union.

Exports rose sharply by 35.20 per cent in October from the same month last year in US dollar terms, customs data showed on Tuesday, only a touch slower than the 36.30 per cent surge in September, but ahead of economists' forecast for an increase of 33.50 per cent.
That helped lift China's trade surplus to US$1.04 trillion in the first 10 months, topping US$1 trillion for a second consecutive year and reaching the milestone a month earlier than in 2025.

The swelling surplus could fuel further tensions with the European Union, where leaders have called for more trade curbs with China after reaching an agreement with Beijing to limit Chinese exports of hybrid vehicles to the bloc over the next few years.
Because the measures have yet to take effect, factories are expected to bring forward shipments, bolstering exports in the near term.

China on Monday officially announced the extension of a trade truce with Washington due to expire on Nov 10 by two months, but said last week that expanding its purchases of US farm goods would hinge on the implementation of their agreed reciprocal tariff-reduction arrangement.

"The risk of additional tariffs and other trade barriers will remain elevated in 2027, particularly as Chinese manufacturers continue expanding their presence in overseas markets," said Joe Peissel, lead macroeconomist at Trivium China.
Imports grew 41.60 per cent, beating the median forecast for a 32 per cent increase in the Reuters poll and accelerating from the 31 per cent growth in September.

The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit will take place next week in the southern Chinese tech and innovation hub of Shenzhen, where Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump are expected to meet for the third time so far this year.
HEADWINDS AND UNCERTAINTIES
One big worry for Beijing is that consumers remain reluctant to spend, constrained by a property market downturn that has battered household wealth and dented confidence in the economic outlook.
Sluggish demand at home has pushed Chinese automakers to seek sales in overseas markets.
China's car exports maintained a solid pace of growth in October, while domestic vehicle sales recorded a 12th straight month of declines, separate data released by an industry association showed.
Greater reliance on exports, however, leaves China's economy increasingly exposed to any slowdown in global demand.
Much of the strength in exports this year has been fuelled by a global push to expand AI infrastructure.

"The outlook for exports depends on how long the AI boom will last," Macquarie analysts wrote. They expect China's exports to accelerate further in the fourth quarter before starting to slow from the first quarter of 2027.

3fde928bb7a7ca6f: SAN FRANCISCO, Nov 10 — Anthropic announced yesterday that it would release updated versions of two of its most powerful artificial intelligence (AI) models as the company prepares for a highly anticipated IPO this month.
The new models, Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, can perform up to 30 per cent faster than previous versions, particularly on complex tasks such as coding, while costing 20 per cent less, the company said.
Both are built on the same underlying model. Fable 5.2 has safeguards that block most cybersecurity and biology tasks, which lets Anthropic offer it to all users.
Mythos 5.2 has fewer of those restrictions and is available only to vetted organisations working in cybersecurity or biomedical research.
The first versions of Fable and Mythos were released under a cloud of controversy.

Both models were pulled days after their June launch, when the US Commerce Department, citing national security concerns, ordered Anthropic to bar access by foreign nationals. The controls were lifted weeks later.

The latest versions come as Anthropic is aiming to hold its initial public offering the week of November 16, when it is expected to raise up to US$100 billion (RM405 billion), which would make it the largest IPO on record.
The San Francisco-based lab’s Wall Street debut is expected to fetch a valuation exceeding US$1 trillion, though estimates have fallen in recent weeks from a high of US$2 trillion.
The stock market debut is being seen as a gauge of how long the AI spending boom lifting the US economy can last.
Growth has been staggering at the company. Anthropic’s revenue reached US$17 billion in the third quarter, up from just US$1.4 billion a year earlier, a securities filing showed earlier this month.
Sales growth slowed from previous quarters, however, amid fierce competition from ChatGPT-maker OpenAI and cheaper models, many of them from China.
Anthropic also posted an operating loss of US$567 million in the third quarter as it paid more for short-term computing capacity.
The company’s valuation has also been weighed down by a broader market pullback after a string of quarterly earnings reports spooked investors.
These raised concerned about the hundreds of billions of dollars that US tech giants are spending on AI.
Democrats also regained control of Congress in the US midterms, raising investor concerns about a potential regulatory crackdown on the tech industry, including against data centre buildouts.
Ballot measures restricting data centre construction could hamper the growth plans of AI developers such as Anthropic, as well as rivals including OpenAI, Meta, Microsoft and Google. — AFP

41e76b373c3188c2: SYDNEY: Papua New Guinea is considering ways to limit families to just three children in a bid to stop its booming population from overwhelming public services, Prime Minister James Marape said.

China for decades enforced a "one child" policy to curb population growth before ending it in 2016, while nations such as Vietnam and Iran have experimented with measures to limit families to two kids.
Official figures rank Papua New Guinea among the fastest growing countries in the world, although census data is notoriously unreliable in the South Pacific nation.
Marape said limiting families to three children would "curtail uncontrolled demographic expansion".
"This is to ensure that there is prevention of unplanned pregnancies and births, and families will be encouraged to have no more than three children," he said on Monday while touring a hospital.
It was not immediately clear what Marape's family planning policy would entail.
Papua New Guinea has an official population of around 10 million people.
But some analysts suggest the figure could be much higher, given difficulties counting people scattered throughout the nation's dense forests and rugged hills.

The Papua New Guinea government statistics office has estimated the average yearly population growth rate at 2.6%, while the National Research Institute of Papua New Guinea says recent growth is around 3%.
The UAE has the highest population growth rate in the world at 4.7%, according to the World Bank.
27a0314d91dd76bf: WASHINGTON, Nov 10 — Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) chief Dana White turned down President Donald Trump’s — apparently jovial — offer of a job as press secretary in a surprise appearance at the White House yesterday.
Trump stunned the world by saying on social media on Saturday that he had asked White to take on the high-profile post — but a day later the 80-year-old president said he was “only kidding.”
The 57-year-old cage fighting boss visited the White House on Monday, and Trump brought him out for a chaotic news conference in the James Brady Briefing Room.
“So let me ask you the big question. Would you like to be press secretary of the United States of America? Or do you just want to stay with this ridiculous UFC? Huh?” Trump said.
“Thank you for the offer, sir — for the offer, I have no, no — I do not want to be in politics,” White replied.
Trump smiled and headed out of the room, saying: “I am devastated to hear this. Goodbye, everybody.”

The press secretary’s post has been vacant since Katie Zacharia left on October 16 after less than a week in the post. Her combative predecessor Karoline Leavitt left in August after a year and a half in the job.

Trump’s announcement that he had offered the high-profile job to “violent Fighter and Warrior” White had sparked speculation that he was ready for a aggressive stance after the Republican Party’s stunning midterm elections defeat.
White is a long-time friend of the president and helped host a massive UFC match on the White House lawn earlier this year.
But there was also some skepticism about the president’s announcement, and Trump said Sunday night that he had been joking.
Leading out White to the podium yesterday, Trump said he had been “having a little fun.”
“He’s a great guy,” Trump told the room full of reporters. “The only problem is he’ll talk for a little while and then he’s going to beat the hell out of you.”
Standing at the lectern and wearing a black t-shirt and jacket, White looked like he might be more comfortable in the octagon — the ring used for UFC fights.
“I’ve always wanted to do this. Who has the first question?” he joked — before quickly adding: “I have zero political aspirations.”
White added that “the last 24 hours of my life has been insane” since Trump made the announcement.

Asked by a journalist to confirm he had said no to the job, White added: “I don’t tell the president ‘no’ to anything... I didn’t want to be disrespectful and say anything until he said something first.”

Trump then took a series of questions on more weighty matters, from the Iran and Ukraine wars to the possible impeachment of Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth and a spy scandal engulfing Nvidia boss Jensen Huang. — AFP
