347a4629baae3b09: MELAKA, Nov 10 — The interpretation of the Conditional Pardon Order and the implications of the Order of Discharge involving Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak require further clarification to establish whether the Prisons Department has the authority to implement house arrest for the former prime minister.
Home Affairs Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the department, as the implementing agency, needed to ensure that its actions did not result in wrongful detention.

“We are the implementing agency. The Order of Discharge states that he is to be released, whereas the Pardons Board refers to house arrest. House arrest is different from release. So, from our position, which one should we follow? These are legal documents and if there is any ambiguity, we refer the matter to the court.

“The wording used is ‘discharge forthwith’, meaning release. In prison terminology, there are distinctions between release, discharge and discharge not amounting to acquittal. If discharge means that he is released, then the Prisons Department no longer has any authority over him. But if it is house arrest, the department still has authority,” he told reporters.

Saifuddin was commenting on a statement by the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) last Friday that the implementation of house arrest for Najib had been temporarily deferred pending further examination of the Conditional Pardon Order and the implications of the Order of Discharge issued by the High Court in Kuala Lumpur, following the settlement of the RM50 million fine.
Elaborating, he said the Order of Discharge was issued by the Registrar of the High Court, prompting the ministry to seek the AGC’s views on the matter.

“Who issued this Order of Discharge? It was issued by the Registrar of the High Court. That is why we sought the AGC’s views and, as explained, the matter will be brought before the court to clarify the two differing interpretations,” he said.
He said he had no information on which party would bring the matter before the court or when a decision would be made.

“However, I wish to stress that this is purely a matter of interpretation. We comply with, respect and accept the notification of the house arrest order for Najib, as stated in the letter sent by the Secretary of the Pardons Board to the Home Ministry,” he said.

Saifuddin was speaking after attending an engagement and dialogue session with fishermen at the Lereh Tanjung Kling Fishermen’s Jetty here yesterday, which was also attended by Malaysian Fisheries Development Authority (LKIM) chairman Muhammad Faiz Fadzil.
In an earlier statement, the AGC said Najib would remain at his current place of detention throughout the period of deferment, subject to the authority and directions of the relevant authorities.
Najib paid the RM50 million fine imposed on him in the SRC International funds misappropriation case at the High Court Criminal Registry Office last Friday. — Bernama
57c16a375f1efd55: JERUSALEM, Nov 10 — He built his career on unyielding principles, but the Israeli secular nationalist Avigdor Liberman is now preaching compromise in a bid to bring down Benjamin Netanyahu, his former mentor whom he now despises.
For three decades, Liberman’s steely blue eyes, steadily greying whiskers and ample use of chess metaphors have been an ever-present part of Israeli political life.
So too has been the unwavering defence of secularism by the 68-year-old immigrant from the former Soviet Union, as religious Jews gain political influence inside Israel.

But it is towards ultra-Orthodox Jews, derided as draft-dodgers by his political base, that Liberman is now extending a hand, in the service of what he considers an even greater goal — removing Netanyahu.

Liberman, who shares Netanyahu’s hawkish worldview and antipathy to the idea of a Palestinian state, was credited with helping first bring the prime minister to power in his razor-thin 1996 election upset.

Liberman served as Netanyahu’s first chief of staff. But as Netanyahu rose to become Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, in power on and off for nearly 20 years, Liberman turned into a staunch critic.

Years before the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack and Israel’s massive retaliation in Gaza that brought Netanyahu international notoriety, Liberman advocated such total war and accused Netanyahu of being too hesitant.

Liberman resigned as Netanyahu’s defence minister in 2018 to protest the government’s acceptance of a previous ceasefire with Hamas. Liberman has also lashed out at Netanyahu for tacitly backing Qatari funding to keep Gaza afloat before the Hamas attack.
U-turn on ultra-Orthodox

A resident of one of the West Bank’s settlements, which are illegal under international law, Liberman is, like Netanyahu, a vociferous critic of the Palestinian Authority, the semi-autonomous, European-supported body set up in the 1990s under the Oslo peace accords.

During the latest election campaign, Liberman called for Jordan to retake control of the parts of the West Bank now under Palestinian Authority administration, saying it was the most practical option.
The stance sparked a furious rebuke from Netanyahu, who has flirted with annexing the West Bank and accused his foe of letting a foreign army “rule over territories in the land of Israel”.

Liberman also fell out with Netanyahu over the premier’s alliance with the ultra-Orthodox, who have been allowed an exemption to Israel’s usually mandatory military service, angering many Israelis at a time when reservists are serving multiple tours of duty.
But last week, Liberman stunned his party by announcing he was lifting a veto on working with the ultra-Orthodox and saying he was ready for a compromise on military service.
Liberman remains adamantly opposed to working with lawmakers from Israel’s Arab minority, who have enough votes to put in power opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot.
Liberman’s Yisrael Beiteinu party won seven seats, the fewest among the core opposition parties, but every vote is critical for Eisenkot.

Russian immigrant base
Born in Soviet Moldova, Liberman immigrated to Israel in 1978, serving in the military before working for a time as a nightclub bouncer and studying political science.

He was originally part of Netanyahu’s Likud party, but in 1999 founded Yisrael Beiteinu, which means “Israel Our Home”, to appeal to the more than one million Israelis who had immigrated from the former Soviet Union.

Responding to speculation regarding his about-face on the ultra-Orthodox, Liberman blamed lingering prejudice against Russian speakers, who have become increasingly integrated since mass immigration in the 1990s.

“I have been witnessing a parade of foolishness by a string of commentators, journalists acting on behalf of vested interests, bots and people with prejudiced views, sometimes with a distinctly racist undertone,” Liberman wrote in a series of defiant social media posts.

Some commentators speculated that Liberman, whose base has expanded beyond Russian-speaking immigrants, was seeking a political deadlock that would then make him the consensus candidate. He denied he was seeking to become prime minister himself.
“I am not engaged in political manoeuvring, nor am I trying to undermine anyone,” Liberman said.

Liberman said there was no choice but compromise, even though he has previously called the ultra-Orthodox “anti-Jewish” for refusing military service and denounced an ultra-Orthodox rally last year against conscription as “spit in the face of our heroic soldiers”. — AFP

77e567663b226790: SINGAPORE: Asian stocks rose on Tuesday as a drop in oil prices after US president Donald Trump said he plans to hold off on new military strikes against Iran lifted sentiment ahead of US inflation data that could sway the near-term interest rate outlook.

Brent crude futures were hovering at their lowest levels since early September, well below US$100 per barrel, as investors pinned their hopes on possible talks between US and Iran. They were last down 1% at US$91.56 a barrel.
The US-Israeli war with Iran, which erupted at the end of February, has stoked inflationary concerns across the globe, spurring major central banks to raise rates in recent months.

Nick Twidale, chief market strategist at ATFX Global, said the latest developments offered hope that an end to the conflict could be approaching, but there was still a considerable gap between diplomacy and a lasting peace agreement.

"The risk now is that markets have moved too far, too quickly... any indication that negotiations are faltering could see a substantial rebound in prices as traders rapidly rebuild the geopolitical risk premium," he said.

The slump in oil prices eased inflation worries and helped lift stocks after last week's rout as a sweeping victory by Democrats in the US midterm elections fed concerns that new regulations could dent the durability of the AI trade.

South Korea's KOSPI rose over 5%, while Japan's Nikkei gained about 3% in early trading. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares pushed 1.5% higher, moving away from the seven-month low it hit last week.
On Monday, the S&P 500 clocked its biggest one-day jump since April, closing up 2.35% while the Nasdaq closed 2.7% higher, its best day in over four months.
"We believe resets in expectations are healthy, and the AI trade appears to be working through a reset of its own at the moment," said Anthony Saglimbene, chief market strategist at Ameriprise.
Earnings reports due this week from tech companies including CoreWeave, a barometer of investor anxiety over AI, will be another test for markets as investors fret about the cost of the AI buildout.
Saglimbene said Anthropic's prospective IPO could be an important test of investor confidence.
Nvidia remains at the centre of storm
Market focus remains on Nvidia after the second-most valuable company in the world said its board was probing whether CEO Jensen Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence operation.

A media report alleged he had a close relationship with a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to Beijing. Huang has said he was unfaithful to his wife without disclosing details. Shares of Nvidia, which is due to report earnings next week, fell 4.2%.

Daniel Morgan, portfolio manager at Synovus Trust, said certain personalities in the technology space were so intertwined with the success of the company it was hard to separate the two. Morgan holds Nvidia shares.

"But, the companies can still be successful long after the original founders have taken on a lesser role," he said, adding he remained confident that Nvidia would continue to maintain its lead in the GPU AI chip market even if Huang was forced to step down to a lesser role.
Inflation data sets up rates outlook

All eyes will be on US inflation data later in the day, with prices likely to have increased at a moderate pace in October, economists said, and remaining stubbornly high enough for the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates next month.
Economists polled by Reuters expect headline consumer prices to have risen 0.3% last month, with core prices posting a 0.2% increase.
Traders are pricing in an 84% chance of a rate hike next month versus 74% a week earlier, a CME FedWatch tool showed after a blowout October jobs report on Friday.
The 2-year note yield, which typically moves in step with Fed interest rate expectations, was 1.4 basis points higher to 4.56%. The US dollar was steady in Asian hours.

e23b472a101e117c: ALOR GAJAH, Nov 10 — Gadek has the potential to become a hub for modern agriculture and livestock farming, creating job opportunities for local youths and reducing their need to seek employment elsewhere, particularly in Singapore.
Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate for the Gadek state seat, Jegasilan K, 45, said the area still had vast tracts of land that could be developed for modern vegetable cultivation and livestock farming.
He said former rubber plantations could be transformed into agricultural areas producing various crops for local markets, alongside livestock hubs for poultry and cattle.
“As a local, I see considerable potential to expand modern agriculture in the villages around Gadek, particularly through livestock farming and vegetable cultivation.
“We can introduce various crops that can penetrate local markets while developing poultry and cattle farming hubs here,” he told Bernama.
Jegasilan, who runs a tuition centre, said local youths could spearhead these initiatives if given appropriate training and guidance.

He said developing local employment opportunities could help reduce the number of young people migrating to Singapore, where working away from home often made it difficult for them to return during emergencies and festive occasions.
Apart from agriculture, he said Gadek also had potential to become a tourism destination, citing its waterfalls, hot springs, accommodation facilities and other natural attractions.
He said these attractions could be further developed by tapping the ideas and abilities of local youths.
On his campaign, Jegasilan said he had received encouraging responses from Malay, Chinese and Indian residents during his house-to-house visits over the past week.

He said water supply, drainage and road conditions were among the issues frequently raised, while residents also wanted an elected representative who remained approachable and accessible after taking office.
“They do not want a ‘weekly representative’, but someone who remains close to the people and is easy to reach whenever problems arise,” he said.
Jegasilan faces three challengers in the Gadek state seat contest — S. Nadarajah of Barisan Nasional (BN), Laveen Balaprabhakaran (Bersama) and Laila Norinda Maon (Putra).
Polling is set for November 14, with early voting on November 10.

509c77426fa516fa: SYDNEY: Artificial intelligence companies will have to abide by new "mandatory" safeguards when operating in Australia, prime minister Anthony Albanese said Tuesday.
Global unease about the power of advanced AI is growing after a string of hacking incidents involving leading companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic.
Australia would establish a new AI safety regulator tasked with implementing measures designed to keep the booming industry in check, Albanese said.
"Our task is to make sure that we shape AI, rather than AI shape us," Albanese told reporters.
"You can't turn it off and pretend it isn't happening. But what we can do is make sure you shape it in Australia's interest."
The measures would include "mandatory" reporting of AI security breaches and the independent evaluation of frontier AI models, Albanese said.
"Australia is a first mover in this space and we want to make sure that we reap the potential benefits of AI," said Albanese.
"But we need to ensure that we get it right, and social licence is absolutely critical."
Australia voiced deep unease earlier this year after a prototype OpenAI model bypassed safeguards during training and hacked into a government website.
The model sought access to a health statistics portal in June, sidestepping restrictions to breach a section hosting private files.
OpenAI did not raise the alarm with the Australian government until September, when it sent a message to a generic email inbox that is only checked once each day.
Can't 'run away'
Defence minister Richard Marles said AI companies should open themselves to external scrutiny to make sure their tools are safe.
"There needs to be greater risk management of AI capabilities," he told reporters.
"It's important that there is independent assessment of AI models."
Marles said it was pointless to pretend that AI would not reshape the world.
"This is not a technology that we can run away from.
"AI is part of our lives today and it will only grow as part of our lives going forward."
With immense renewable energy potential and vast stretches of uninhabited land, Australia has billed itself as a prime location for the data centres needed to power artificial intelligence.
OpenAI is involved in the construction of a massive data centre on the outskirts of Sydney.
But AI companies also face a growing local backlash, as many Australians question their ethics and the environmental footprint of their power-hungry data hubs.
A major point of contention is whether Australia will water down its copyright laws so that chatbots can be trained on songs, books and other works of art.
e84f1d485d7d4933: NEW YORK, Nov 10 — AI chip behemoth Nvidia was plunged into turmoil yesterday after CEO Jensen Huang acknowledged having an affair, with reports saying US officials believe the woman was spying for China.
Beijing denied the claim, but shares of the chipmaker tumbled after Nvidia’s board opened an inquiry into reports that Huang had been “the target of a foreign intelligence effort.”
Nvidia shares closed more than four per cent lower, after being down nearly nine per cent earlier in the session.

Late last month, The New York Times reported that US intelligence officials had determined Alice Huang, a Chinese executive linked to Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed, had been funnelling information to Beijing.
The executive, also known as Huang Le and no relation to 63-year-old Taiwanese-born Jensen Huang, developed a close relationship with him, the Times said.
In a message to Nvidia employees released on Sunday, Jensen Huang admitted he had been “unfaithful” to his wife.
“My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry,” he said.

Jensen Huang is a central figure in the AI boom and a close informal adviser to US President Donald Trump, who has repeatedly opposed regulating the industry so as not to let China gain the upper hand.
Trump told reporters that he had spoken with Nvidia’s chief yesterday and that he was “suffering greatly.”
“I asked him that question, ‘did you have any idea that she was a spy?’ He said ‘I had no idea that she was a spy,’ and I really believe him,” Trump told a White House press briefing.
The Times said Alice Huang’s relationship with the Nvidia chief could have given her insights into Trump’s thinking around AI.
Foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun told a regular briefing Monday that “the narrative of a so-called Chinese spy is entirely baseless vilification and smearing.”
AI is likely to come up when Trump meets President Xi Jinping later this month at a summit in China.
‘You never know’
Asked Sunday whether Huang would join the president’s Asia trip, which includes the Asia-Pacific summit in Shenzhen, Trump told reporters: “I don’t know but I’ll certainly take him.”
Nvidia’s board said in a statement Sunday it had opened an independent probe “in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.”
“While the board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the board’s inquiry will examine all available information,” it said.
China is in a race for tech dominance against the United States, which restricts the export to China of the most cutting-edge silicon chips.
Nvidia, a global leader in producing chips used to train and run AI models, is one of the world’s most valuable companies.
Megaspeed was under scrutiny for possibly steering Nvidia AI chips to China, the Times report said, citing unnamed sources briefed on the matter.
Trump was briefed on the intelligence findings about Huang’s relationship with the businesswoman roughly a year ago and chose not to act on the information, the Times report said.
Trump said Sunday that he did not regret not acting on this intelligence, calling Huang “an honourable guy.”
‘Black eye moment’
Technology analyst Dan Ives, with the investment bank Yorkville Ives, said the inquiry was “a black eye moment” for Jensen Huang.
He predicted it would at the very least spark multiple congressional inquiries and “create an overhang on the stock for a myriad of reasons.”
In the near term, Huang is expected to keep his job but risks being removed as Nvidia’s CEO depending on the findings of the inquiry, Ives said.

George Chen, partner and chair of digital practice at The Asia Group, told AFP “it would be premature to conclude that Jensen poses a threat to US national security before the facts are fully established.”
“Once you become famous, you will naturally become a target,” Chen said.

The House Select Committee on China last week asked Huang to appear in Washington on November 18 for a “closed-door briefing on Nvidia’s security protocols,” according to a letter posted on X that cited reports about Alice Huang. — AFP

f906ed02e2c7b610: PETALING JAYA: A lawyer representing Najib Razak has claimed that the Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC) is shifting the goalposts at the eleventh hour regarding the implementation of the house arrest order for the former prime minister.
Farhan Shafee said Attorney-General Dusuki Mokhtar’s statement yesterday demonstrated a shift in position from the AGC’s earlier media statement, which had caused confusion.
"So, which is it? Is the AGC saying that there are two possible interpretations or that the order itself is defective? These are two different complaints, each with its own remedy.
"It is difficult for us to provide a precise answer when the party making these statements keeps moving the goalposts and changing its position," Berita Harian reported him saying.

Farhan also said the order of discharge issued by the Kuala Lumpur High Court clearly stated that the RM50 million fine had been paid and that the remainder of Najib’s sentence was to be served under house arrest in accordance with the conditional pardon.

"There is nothing in the order that requires interpretation," he said, adding that all parties should understand that court orders in criminal cases are prepared and issued by the court itself, unlike in civil cases where they are prepared by the defence.
Yesterday, Dusuki questioned the care taken in preparing court documents relating to the implementation of Najib’s house arrest order.
He said there were "obvious" defects in the order of discharge relating to the former prime minister’s sentence in the SRC International corruption case.
The alleged defects, which raised questions among legal practitioners, reportedly involve the accuracy of the terminology and legal provisions used in the document.

The High Court issued the order of discharge after the RM50 million fine imposed on the former Umno president was paid through a solidarity fund launched by the party, paving the way for him to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.

However, the AGC subsequently moved to defer the implementation of Najib’s house arrest pending a review of the conditional pardon and order of discharge. It said these issues involved "complex legal questions" that had implications for the execution of the royal pardon and a court order.
The AGC said its request was not an attempt to dispute the conditional pardon, but to clarify the legal effect of the discharge order.
Its decision drew criticism from Istana Negara, which said any arguments challenging the conditional pardon order for Najib amounted to defying the Yang di-Pertuan Agong’s decree.
Istana Negara maintained that the pardon order was clear, explicit and unambiguous, and had no bearing on any other cases faced by Najib.

Perisytiharan berkenaan berkuat kuasa pada tarikh tersebut.

'Orang yang dalam jagaan sah' ialah Najib Razak dengan alamat tertera ialah kediamannya. Ertinya rumah Najib sekarang ialah sebuah penjara. Menteri yang disebut dalam perisytiharan itu ialah Menteri Dalam Negeri Saifuddin Nasution.
Tidak ada huraian atau penjelasan lanjut Kementerian Dalam Negeri khususnya agensinya Jabatan Penjara. AGC juga tidak memberi keterangan mengiringi perisytiharan itu.

“In the case of this Taman Duta Prison, it seems that immediate family members are allowed to share it with the inmate”, kata wartawan veteran A Kadir Jasin menerusi hantaran di Facebook, beberapa hari lalu.
Saya setuju. Menurut dokumen diwartakan seluruh rumah Najib diisytihar penjara, bukan sebahagian. Bukan bilik khas untuk Najib sahaja dijadikan penjara mengurungnya.

Maka, dengan sendirinya semua penghuni yang sememangnya tinggal di banglo mewah di Langgak Duta kekal sebagai penghuni. Ertinya, Rosmah Mansor, isteri Najib, bersama anggota keluarga terdekat akan bersama Najib dalam 'penjara' Langgak Duta. Begitu juga pembantu rumah dan sebagainya (kalau ada).

Ini keadaan berbeza dengan apa yang dikenakan oleh pemerintah Myanmar ke atas bekas pemimpin negara itu, Aung San Suu Kyi. Beliau dipindahkan dari penjara ke sebuah rumah untuk menjalani baki hukuman tahanan rumah.

Tetapi, kediaman itu bukan rumah Suu Kyi. Lokasi tidak didedah kepada umum. Sinar Harian memetik akhbar The Irrawaddy melaporkan Suu Kyi ditempatkan di sebuah rumah khas dengan kawalan keselamatan di Naypyidaw yang terletak di kawasan kediaman keluarga tentera dan dikelilingi pagar tinggi.
Hubungan Suu Kyi dengan dunia luar sangat terbatas. Pasukan peguamnya dilapor tidak dibenarkan bertemunya secara bersemuka, sejak Disember 2022.
Pada hemat saya, boleh dikatakan Suu Kyi tinggal sebagai tahanan rumah 'incommunicado' - berseorangan.

Bagi Najib, pelawat dibenarkan dengan syarat mendapat izin terlebih dahulu secara bertulis pihak berkuasa dan dikehendaki melalui 'security screening' mengikut prosidur biasa Jabatan Penjara. Ini saya nyatakan berdasar laporan media seperti kata Kadir.
“This whole unprecedented operation will cost tax payers additional money,” katanya.
Ikut logik, Najib sebagai seorang banduan tidak boleh memiliki atau memegang telefon bimbit atau apa-apa alat komunikasi. Namun, pada pandangan saya beliau tidak perlu itu semua.
Sebab beliau boleh jika mahu menyampaikan salam dan pesanan kepada kawan, sahabat handai, sanak-saudara, sesiapa sahaja melalui Rosmah atau anggota keluarga.
Yang kena tahan Najib bukan Rosmah. Lantas beliau dan ahli keluarga yang tinggal serumah dengan Najib bebas keluar masuk berjumpa siapa saja di luar.

Justeru, Najib boleh (saya ulangi) kalau mahu, 'run Umno' daripada rumah, beri nasihat, dan atur strategi untuk parti berdepan pilihan raya misalnya. 'Work from home'. Silap. 'It should be control from home'.
Cuma, jangan sampai Umno merasa mereka ada dua presiden. Sekadar 'friendly reminder'.

Antara ciri utama konsep tahanan antarabanga banyak negara termasuk Singapura, New Zealand, dan Australia menggunakan peranti pemantauan elektronik atau gelang kaki GPS atau sistem biometrik untuk mengesan pergerakan tahanan dari jarak jauh.

Tidak dapat dipasitkan sama ada ia akan digunakan untuk Najib. Yang pasti, beliau boleh buat apa sahaja dan bergerak dalam rumah. Yakni, bebas bergaul dengan keluarga dan bergerak asalkan dalam rumah.
Untuk memastikan Najib berada dalam rumah sepanjang masa ialah tanggunjawab pegawai penjara. Penjara walaupun banglo mewah mestilah dijaga oleh pegawai penjara. Nama pun penjara.

Maka, tentulah akan ada beberapa syif 24 jam setiap hari. Tidak tahu berapa pegawai bertugas setiap satu syif. Tidak tahu berapa ramai pegawai terlibat. Setakat ini, belum ada apa apa pengumuman mengenai perkara itu.

Pasti pegawai penjara dalam satu syif yang sama perlu dibawa ulang-alik dengan kenderaan jabatan dari Penjara Kajang atau Sungai Buloh untuk bertugas di 'penjara' Langgak Duta. Bak kata Kadir 'a set of prison guards would have to be assigned to it'.

Dan, adakah pegawai penjara boleh masuk ke dalam rumah untuk membuat kawalan atau mengawal Najib? 'From the inside?' atau mereka hanya dibolehkan mengawal luar rumah? Mungkin kerana tidak mahu mengganggu privasi anggota keluarga Najib?
Di penjara biasa makanan untuk banduan yakni sarapan pagi, makan tengah hari, makan malam disediakan pihak penjara. Bagaimana pula di penjara 'luar biasa' di kawasan elit Langgak Duta?
Makan penjara 'biasa' dibawa masuk atau Najib boleh nikmati quinoa, ikan baung tempoyak ala hidangan Terengganu dan lain-lain kegemarannya yang dimasak di dapur Langgak Duta?
Cukup disini meskipun ada banyak persoalan yang timbul. Umpamanya yang diutarakan kolumnis FMT Tajuddin Rasdi yang disiar semalam.
Apa pun Najib masih di penjara Kajang berikutan pengangguhan sementara AGC berhubung pelaksanaan tahanan rumah untuknya.
Kita tunggu saja perkembangaan seterusnya.

350cd2b042e00eb8: SINGAPORE, Nov 9 — SoftBank Group Corp and Grab Holdings Ltd yesterday announced the signing of joint development agreements in connection with plans for US$1.85 billion (RM7.5 billion) initial combined seed capital to develop artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure in Malaysia with Petroleum Sarawak Bhd (Petros).

In a joint statement, SoftBank and Grab said the combined investment forms part of a multi-year plan to develop AI compute capacity across Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia, with a long-term target of five gigawatts or more.
The proposed initial combined seed capital of US$1.85 billion comprised US$1 billion from SoftBank Group, US$750 million from Grab and US$100 million from Petros.
“The collaboration aimed to establish AI infrastructure in Malaysia to meet the growing demand for computing capacity across Southeast Asia and globally.

“Once fully operational, the facilities are expected to be amongst the largest AI infrastructure of their kind in Asia, providing governments, multinational companies and small businesses with reliable access to advanced computing capabilities,” they said.
According to the statement, the proposed investment will be deployed in stages subject to projects achieving key development and customer contract milestones, and the necessary closing conditions.

Grab co-founder, chairman and chief executive officer Anthony Tan said the company and SoftBank plan to build critical AI infrastructure in Malaysia, where Grab began, for all of Southeast Asia region.
“This infrastructure will allow us to accelerate the development of localised AI solutions for our communities.

“Through this partnership, we can drive faster regional AI development and adoption, bringing its transformative benefits to many millions of people, while contributing to Malaysia’s economy through the creation of high-value jobs and AI upskilling,” he said.

The statement said the projects will be developed in close collaboration with Malaysia’s Federal Government and the Sarawak government, aligning with the National AI Action Plan 2026-2030 (AI Nation 2030) to position Malaysia as an inclusive and sustainable AI nation, as well as Sarawak’s long-term development aspiration under the Post Covid-19 Development Strategy 2030.
The facilities will operate in line with Malaysia’s renewable energy use guidelines, and feature high-efficiency infrastructure designed to reduce water use and reliance on local power grids.
“Beyond AI infrastructure development, the parties will explore other areas of mutual interest, including advanced manufacturing in Malaysia.

“These initiatives are expected to create high-value employment opportunities in engineering, design and technical fields, while supporting the objectives of the National Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) Policy and the Malaysia Digital Economy Blueprint (MDEB).
“They will also help accelerate advanced technology adoption, improve productivity and strengthen the capabilities of Malaysia’s workforce,” it added. — Bernama
f37660ec34da2ea7: RAMALLAH: The United Nations (UN) and the Palestinian Authority have warned that the coming winter could exacerbate the humanitarian crisis in the Gaza Strip, reported German Press Agency (dpa).
More than two million people rely on shelter and aid, officials said at a press conference in the West Bank city of Ramallah on Monday.
Sameh Hamad, the Palestinian Authority’s social development minister, said hundreds of thousands of their people still live in tents and temporary shelters following Israel’s bombardment.
He said 84% of the population was housed in overcrowded emergency shelters, while more than 65% of families live in tents and temporary shelters.
More than 65,000 tents and emergency shelters are threatened by or already affected by flooding, Hamad said, citing UN figures.
He added thousands of families live in some 4,000 buildings at risk of collapse, with no safer alternative.
UN emergency relief coordinator Ramiz Alakbarov said the crisis had been caused by human action, emphasising that Israeli import restrictions had hampered preparations for the winter.
Alakbarov urged Israel to urgently lift restrictions on imports of urgently needed aid and equipment.
The population must also be allowed into more areas of the territory with safer shelters, he said.

The Israeli military said it has been conducting "a winter preparedness plan" in coordination with the Board of Peace, established by US president Donald Trump, and in cooperation with the UN, international organisations and donor countries.
It said more than 91,000 tents and more than 8,200 trucks carrying tarpaulins, blankets, winter clothing and other aid had already been brought into the Gaza Strip.
7cd693f250941a73: SYDNEY: The dollar found support following a bumpy few days and held firm in Tuesday's Asia session while traders waited for US inflation data, which could push it higher if it bolsters rate hike bets.
A tumble in oil prices and gains overnight for stocks had knocked the dollar lower as investors rotated back into riskier assets.

The trade and sentiment-sensitive Australian dollar rose by nearly 1% through Monday to sit at US$0.6921 early on Tuesday and the New Zealand dollar rose even further to trade at US$0.5624, with both steady in morning Asia trade.

The euro jumped 0.7% overnight to US$1.1220, reversing a Friday fall when strong US jobs data lifted the dollar and interest rate expectations, and putting the euro/dollar pair roughly into the middle of a range it has held for a month.

The market is long dollars and the dollar index has gained this year as early expectations for US interest rate cuts quickly turned to bets on hikes after the US-Israeli war on Iran drove up energy prices and fuelled inflation.
A blowout October jobs report on Friday, with hiring more than twice forecasts, has markets pricing an 85% chance of a Federal Reserve rate increase next month.

Headline inflation is seen picking up to 3.9% and core to 2.8%, year-on-year, in October, according to economists polled by Reuters, so anything hotter than that will add to rate hike expectations and probably lift the dollar, analysts said.
"You can only put a little bit more (in the price) in December, but the price for meetings into the future could go higher," said Imre Speizer, strategist at Westpac in Auckland.

Markets have priced two US hikes by the middle of next year, though the outlook has dimmed somewhat amid the recent turbulence in AI stocks on fears a Democratic sweep of Congress could lead to tighter regulation and slow the AI boom.
"This could be a factor that slows US growth in 2027 and helps put a top in for the dollar," said Macquarie strategists Thierry Wizman and Gareth Berry in a note to clients.

Sterling, which has drawn support since the Bank of England hiked interest rates for the first time in three years last week, sat in the middle of a range it has traded in for almost a year and a half at US$1.3441.
Japan's yen hovered at 157.97 per dollar, having been the best-performing G10 currency against the greenback over the past six months on the back of heavy official intervention.

Figures on Monday showed Japan sold US$97 billion in reserves defending the yen through late July and August as it traversed four-decade lows on the dollar. The threat of further dollar sales is keeping the currency steady, even as expectations for a December rate hike in Japan have lately faded.

42bc912dc85d4181: Seperti parti politik di mana-mana negara termasuklah Malaysia, mempunyai parti yang memperjuangkan berbagai ideologi. Dengan ideologi ini mereka mencari pengikut. Nasionalisme, sosialisme, sekularisme termasuklah membawa idealisme agama. Fahaman ini disebar kepada rakyat agar menyokong agenda mereka yang mereka percaya terbaik untuk semua.

Tetapi, dalam usaha mengekalkan sokongan, manipulasi tetap berlaku. Paling sedap guna agama. Alasan, dalil dan nas dipakai untuk mencari kelebihan ataupun menutup kelemahan sendiri. Pahala, dosa, syurga dan neraka dijadikan modal niaga untuk mengabsahkan tindakan mereka.

Seorang pemimpin politik sebuah parti agama dalam ceramahnya beberapa minggu lalu menjawab kritikan mengapa negeri yang ditadbir oleh mereka selama 36 tahun lambat maju dengan jawapan yang mudah. "Kita bukannya nabi." Senang, kan?

Pasti penyokong mereka terpesona dan kagum dengan jawapan itu. Tiada yang benar melainkan benar belaka hujah itu. Betullah tu, kita bukan nabi, kata penyokong mereka. Kita tak sempurna. Tetapi, bila kerajaan persekutuan atau kerajaan negeri lain yang ditadbir oleh musuh politik mereka lambat, dalam hal banjir di Selangor misalnya apa yang penyokong mereka tak hentam? Kenapa tak letak hujah pemimpin kamu itu kepada keadaan pihak lain?
"Benda bukan boleh selesai sehari dua, kita bukan nabi, kan?"

Terbaru, minggu lalu seorang lagi pemimpin parti itu dalam hantaran yang dibuatnya di Facebook menulis orang yang menderma untuk membantu bekas perdana menteri Najib Razak membayar denda RM50 juta boleh mendapat pahala. Beliau mengaitkan sumbangan itu dan segala bantuan berkaitan dengannya adalah usaha memudahkan urusan. Memudahkan urusan orang dapat pahala. Peh!

Kenyataan ini sangatlah menarik. Bukanlah sebab kita baru sahaja mengetahui bahawa menderma merupakan amalan yang baik dalam Islam. Sejak kecil kita sudah diajar begitu. Masukkan duit ke dalam tabung masjid, bantu anak yatim, beri makan orang miskin, semuanya amalan mulia. Tangan yang di atas lebih baik daripada tangan di bawah. Semua itu telah kita belajar.

Tetapi, apabila derma dikaitkan dengan seorang tokoh politik yang telah disabitkan kesalahan oleh mahkamah, persoalannya menjadi sedikit berbeza. Adakah setiap amalan derma yang kita buat kepada semua pihak itu sama nilainya? Itu yang lebai-lebai politik harus ajar pengikutnya. Selain nilai dan jumlah, perlu dididik juga tujuan sesuatu sumbangan itu apakah ia benar-benar dituntut dalam agama. Apakah ia membantu permasalahan ummah? Apakah akan memberi kebaikan dan keberkatan kepada bangsa, agama dan negara? Dari segi keadilan sejagat, apakah tindakan ini sesuai?

Maaflah, saya tak boleh terima bab seorang ahli politik merasakan dia ada autoriti untuk menentukan seseorang itu boleh mendapat pahala atau dosa. Kalau tolong pihak mereka, dapat pahala. Kalau buat perkara yang sama untuk pihak lain, berdosa. Sewaktu bermusuh habis semua pihak bergelumang dosa. Bila berbaik, kutip dalil untuk menyucikannya. Jika tempat orang ditimpa banjir itu murka Allah, jika tempat mereka kena, itu ujian. Ini amat memalukan jika kita fikir dengan akal yang waras. Saya mahu bertanya, ke mana penyokong kamu hendak dibawa? Barangkali ada segelintir penyokong parti kamu yang berasa malu juga dengan kenyataan ini.

Soal dosa pahala ini bukan perkara yang sedap-sedap jadi bahan mainan. Dalam kehidupan beragama, pahala dan dosa merupakan antara asas yang membentuk pertimbangan manusia. Orang melakukan kebaikan dengan mengharapkan ganjaran tuhan, manakala menjauhi kejahatan kerana takut akan balasan-Nya. Tapi mengapa bagi kamu, pahala dibuat seperti mata ganjaran untuk tebus barang di kedai serbaneka. Kita jadi ahli kedai, dapat kad keahlian, kemudian jika ada tawaran promosi, kita pun beli barang. Daripada pembelian barang, kita dapat 'point' (pahala) yang boleh ditebus kemudiannya. Macam itu? Gila betul.

Begini, biar saya jelaskan. Dalam isu duit denda Najib, saya boleh faham jika ada penyokongnya yang bersungguh-sungguh mahu membantu beliau. Dalam politik, kesetiaan atau ketaasuban bukan sesuatu yang pelik. Semua parti ada penyokong fanatik. Mereka akan bermati-matian mempertahankan pemimpin mereka. Dan dalam isu Najib ini, ada juga yang bersimpati terhadapnya dan ada juga yang mengenang jasa ketika beliau berkuasa lalu mereka pun menderma. Itu hak mereka. Pemimpin parti lain, jika kalah saman pun akan ada penyokong mereka yang bantu buat kutipan dana.

Tetapi, mengusik sentimen penyokong dengan mempergunakan ganjaran pahala ini agak teruk, bagi saya jika kita fikir dalam-dalam. Apakah boleh kita guna 'fatwa' yang sama untuk kutip derma dan permudahkan urusan ratusan bekas banduan yang sudah bebas supaya urusan mereka dipermudahkan? Mereka terpaksa bergelut kesusahan dalam mendapat pekerjaan. Di mana seruan buat pahala kamu? Apakah manusia seperti mereka tak berguna di mata kamu? Bukankah mereka juga berhak kembali ke pangkuan masyarakat untuk menyumbang bakti dan tenaga? Kenapa berpilih-pilih? Di mana keadilannya kalau begitu?

Di luar sana, berapa ramai orang yang memerlukan bantuan untuk membayar kos rawatan, membeli keperluan sekolah anak atau menyelesaikan hutang akibat kesempitan hidup? Berapa ramai rakyat memerlukan air bersih di rumah? Apa usaha dan inisiatif kamu untuk memudahkan urusan mereka? Takkan kepada marhaen asyik dijual pahala dan syurga sahaja demi nak menutup kemalasan kamu berkhidmat? Jika kamu sebagai pentadbir negeri bekerja keras memberikan kemudahan urusan rakyat di bawah kamu, bukankah kamu juga akan mendapat pahala yang besar? Tapi kamu berhelah, 'kita bukan nabi'. Ini sangat teruk!

Apabila seorang ahli politik memakai jubah dan kopiah bercakap tentang pahala, kenyataannya tentulah akan diterima oleh penyokong mereka. Apatah lagi seseorang ahli politik itu mempunyai latar belakang pendidikan agama atau berasal daripada keluarga ulama yang dihormati. Itu akan jadi lebih kuat.

Tetapi, ayuhlah berfikir secara realistik, kita memang tidak tahu apakah dapat pahala atau tidak jika seseorang itu menderma kepada Najib. Jika dapat pun kita tak tahu bagaimana bentuknya, besar mana atau apa rupanya. Itu bukan kita yang tentukan.

Pemimpin yang fatanah seharusnya lebih tahu memilih perkataan sesuai dalam menyampaikan maksudnya. Tetapi, dek kerana miskin kata-kata dan hujah, maka modal niaga paling sesuai ialah menjual agama dan meletakkan pahala di atas meja. Apakah ahli politik merasakan bahawa tuhan memberikan mereka kuasa juga dalam mengagih pahala?
"Kepada sesiapa yang hendak menderma kepada Najib, dibolehkan kerana itu hak anda. Bersimpati, menolong dan memudahkan urusan orang lain adalah amalan yang digalakkan."
Hah! Saya rasa ayat sebegitu sudah cukup. Nampaklah bijak tanpa menanggalkan ciri ‘keustazannya’, kan?

Dalam sinis, saya tetap menganggap menjual pahala dan dosa dalam permainan politik adalah menghina kebijaksanaan rakyat. Kalau ahli politik pun boleh menentukan siapa dapat pahala, alamatnya selepas ini manifesto pilihan raya mungkin tidak lagi menjanjikan pembangunan, pekerjaan atau kos sara hidup yang lebih rendah. Cukuplah dengan janji pahala atau menggunakan alasan 'kita bukan nabi' seperti alasan seorang lagi pemimpin politik parti yang sama.
Malulah sikit. Kalau tak malu dengan tuhan, malulah sikit dengan segelintir penyokong parti kamu sendiri yang lebih bijak daripada kamu. Takkan kamu nampak mereka semua lekeh daripada kamu?
Artikel ini adalah pandangan penulis dan tidak semestinya mewakili FMT.
548b35050a568476: The global race to build artificial intelligence (AI) data centres is entering a politically sensitive phase. Those in the United States just witnessed a massive electoral recoil. The Republican party was thrashed. Badly.
Hence, Malaysia must understand the implications before becoming an alternative destination for facilities facing growing resistance in the United States.
As they head to Malaysia, Putrajaya must understand these data centres come with huge political costs as President Donald Trump has discovered on Nov 3, 2026 in the mid-term election. Why?
For much of Trump’s second administration, the White House has encouraged American technology giants to accelerate investments in AI infrastructure.
The underlying assumption was straightforward.
Whoever controls the largest computing capacity will enjoy a decisive advantage in the development of advanced AI, including potentially super intelligent systems.
Yet technological ambition does not automatically translate into public acceptance.
Across the United States, opposition to hyperscale data centres has grown over electricity consumption, water requirements, noise pollution, land use and the possibility of higher utility bills.
These concerns have become politically significant.
Democratic politicians, including Gina Hinojosa in Texas, Amy Acton in Ohio and Keisha Lance Bottoms in Georgia, have called for pauses on major data centre developments.
Democrats have also discussed congressional investigations into technology companies, raising the prospect of greater scrutiny over the environmental and economic consequences of AI expansion.
The significance extends beyond American domestic politics.
When the world’s largest AI market encounters resistance to physical infrastructure, international investors will reassess where future computing capacity can be built.
Malaysia is an obvious candidate for consideration. International trade and industry minister Johari Ghani is well aware of the risks based on his public statements though.
Malaysia’s geographical position, proximity to Singapore, expanding digital infrastructure and relative political stability make it attractive to multinational technology companies.
Johor has already emerged as a major data centre destination, while investments in Selangor and other states are expanding Malaysia’s digital footprint.

But Malaysia must distinguish between attracting high-quality digital investment and becoming a convenient location for infrastructure that other countries increasingly regard as environmentally burdensome.
A hyperscale data centre is not an ordinary manufacturing facility.
It can consume enormous amounts of electricity continuously, require substantial cooling infrastructure and place additional demands on water resources.
The economic benefits are also uneven.
Construction creates employment, but permanent staffing requirements can be relatively modest compared with the scale of capital invested.
Moreover, expensive imported semiconductor chips and specialised equipment may account for a substantial proportion of investment expenditure.
Malaysia therefore cannot assume that every billion-ringgit investment announced translates into an equivalent expansion of domestic technological capabilities.
The government must ask whether these investments strengthen Malaysia’s AI sovereignty or merely turn the country into a host for foreign-owned computing infrastructure.
This distinction is crucial.

If Malaysian electricity, water and land support AI systems whose intellectual property, strategic decisions and profits remain overwhelmingly overseas, the long-term national benefits may be limited.
Conversely, carefully negotiated investments could strengthen local research, engineering capabilities, cloud services, cybersecurity and the development of Malaysian AI models.
The difference lies in the conditions imposed before approval. Malaysia should require credible assessments of electricity demand, water consumption, grid capacity and environmental sustainability.

It should also establish transparent mechanisms to ensure that ordinary households and small businesses do not indirectly subsidise infrastructure used by exceptionally wealthy technology corporations.
Renewable energy commitments must be verifiable rather than promotional.
Equally important, data centre investments should generate meaningful technology transfers, skilled employment and opportunities for Malaysian universities and enterprises.
Malaysia must avoid repeating the familiar pattern of welcoming foreign capital without sufficiently strengthening domestic technological ownership.
There is also an Asean dimension.
Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand and Vietnam are competing to attract digital investments.
Competition without coordination could encourage governments to offer excessive incentives while overlooking environmental costs.
Asean should instead develop common principles governing sustainable AI infrastructure.
These could include energy efficiency, water security, cybersecurity, data protection and responsible management of increasingly autonomous AI systems.
Malaysia can contribute to such regional discussions while maintaining an investment environment that remains competitive.
The American backlash against hyperscale data centres is not necessarily a rejection of artificial intelligence itself.
It reflects a growing distinction between the benefits promised by AI and the physical costs imposed on communities hosting its infrastructure.
Malaysia should learn from that distinction.
The country needs foreign investment, but it also needs affordable electricity, reliable water supplies, environmental protection and technological independence.
These objectives are not mutually exclusive. They require disciplined planning and regulatory enforcement.
Malaysia should welcome AI investments that deepen its technological capabilities, not simply those seeking cheaper land, electricity and regulatory approval.
The United States is discovering that the infrastructure underpinning AI carries political and social costs.
Malaysia should not wait until those costs become domestic controversies before responding.
The next generation of AI data centres may indeed look increasingly towards Southeast Asia.
Malaysia must ensure that becoming a preferred destination does not mean inheriting problems that others have begun to resist.
Otherwise, the federal and state governments both risk a voters’ revolt as seen in the United States.

efe06b263df6f729: What do discarded batteries from BMW electric vehicles, second-life solar panels and an Orang Asli village deep in the jungles of Pahang have in common? Quite a lot, as I discovered at Kampung Saweh, Pos Sinderut, reached by a 70km jungle trail that takes about two hours to negotiate.

We had volunteered our 4WD vehicles to transport a Universiti Malaya team to the village. This mission was particularly interesting because it combined rural electrification, renewable energy and the reuse of electric vehicle batteries.

As a veteran off-roader, I've spent decades exploring jungle trails and enjoying camping by rivers. These days, one of the more satisfying uses of our 4x4 vehicles is transporting volunteers and equipment to marginalised rural communities.

Leading the project was Tan Chia Kwang, an associate professor, supported by 14 graduate and undergraduate students. The project received funding from Universiti Malaya's community engagement arm, and Ritsumeikan University of Japan, through Shoki Kosai, who is also an associate professor and partner in environmental research.
The initiative brought together academia, industry, and local communities to advance sustainable energy solutions for rural electrification.
Tan had already transported second-life solar panels, electrical wiring, ducts and timber for the Orang Asli villagers to construct solar panel racks and a battery house at Kampung Saweh.

The second-life solar panels were donated by Tech Inspiration Systems, and the students tested them to select healthy units capable of generating upwards of 280 Watts each. But solar panels alone cannot provide reliable electricity after sunset. That's where the battery energy storage system (BESS) comes in.

The battery modules were provided by BMW Malaysia as part of its support for the project, demonstrating the potential of second-life EV battery applications beyond automotive use. These are nickel-cobalt-manganese EV battery modules recovered from warranty replacements.
"I wrote to EV companies in Malaysia seeking partnership for our project. BMW responded and after numerous meetings agreed to support our project,” said Tan.
What the UM team did

Tan explained that his team developed proprietary technology for the project at the smart grid research laboratory of Universiti Malaya's power energy dedicated advanced centre, testing and repurposing battery components before transporting them into the Pahang jungle.
The energy centre, established in 2000, focuses on renewable energy, power electronics, energy storage, smart grids and related technologies.

“The team has developed proprietary technology for this BESS project, with students working late into the night in the lab testing and repurposing battery components before transporting them into the jungle.”

The actual installation was another challenge. Over an intense five days and four nights, the team worked to integrate the solar panels, electrical controls and 30 battery modules. They had to cook their own food -- instant noodles for most of them -- and sleep on the cold floor of the community hall.

The most time-consuming task was wiring the battery modules in what Tan called the "battery house" — a low-carbon bamboo hut built by the villagers. There was something rather appealing about this contrast: sophisticated batteries that once powered premium German EVs now housed in a traditional bamboo structure in the Pahang jungle.
A chance to watch TV

The system will serve 20 Orang Asli households, with each household allocated around 3kWh daily. This allocation is sufficient based on Tan's prior research into rural households’ electricity usage behaviour; Tan has more than 10 years of experience in rural electrification projects.

He said that one of the most important factors for a successful adoption of a battery storage system was engagement with the community. “Over the years, I’ve learnt that it needs several meetings with a Tok Batin and the community to gauge their commitment or adopt another kampung. We’ve been fortunate with this settlement. They’ve contributed more than I expected.”
And what were the villagers most excited about? The opportunity to watch Malaysia's national television channels at night!
It was a reminder that what urban Malaysians take for granted can be a major improvement in the quality of life for isolated rural communities.

However, a standalone solar-battery system cannot provide unlimited electricity supply. Tan has asked the connected households to keep their nightly consumption within an agreed limit, so that the stored energy can not only last through the night but also allow the batteries to achieve their projected lifespan of many years.
There is a bigger story here for Malaysia's rapidly growing EV industry.
Making recycling work

Many EV batteries retain substantial storage capacity even after they are no longer suitable for automotive use. As the data from the US indicates, most have demonstrated around 70% remaining state of health after prolonged service of up to 20 years, although this varies considerably.
Repurposing suitable batteries for stationary energy storage could extend their useful lives by years.

Tan also highlighted a weakness in Malaysia's recycling ecosystem. Some scrap dealers, he said, purchased discarded EV batteries under the mistaken impression that their weight indicated large quantities of valuable recyclable metal.

There are only four companies in Malaysia that are licensed to recycle EV batteries now. Unlike Europe, which is introducing battery passports to improve traceability, Malaysia has yet to establish a comparable comprehensive system.
The Kampung Saweh project demonstrates how properly tested second-life EV batteries can provide useful energy storage instead of prematurely entering the waste stream.

For our volunteer 4x4 transporters from the Land Rover Exchange community, the expedition was another reminder that off-roading needn't be just about adventure. Sometimes, the most satisfying destination is a remote village where a little goodwill, university ingenuity and discarded EV batteries can bring something as simple — and meaningful — as television after sunset.

259ec5bfabf48b67: WASHINGTON: Nvidia chief Jensen Huang, whose chips power the global AI boom and who has the ear of President Donald Trump, has admitted to an affair with a Chinese executive who US intelligence reportedly believes was working for Beijing.
Here is what we know:
What happened?
Huang, 63, acknowledged the relationship Sunday in a message to Nvidia employees.
"I was unfaithful to my wife," he wrote. "My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry."
Huang has been married to his wife Lori since 1985.
His admission followed reports in The New York Times that US intelligence officials had concluded the woman, Alice Huang, was passing information to China. She is not related to the Nvidia chief.
Nvidia had previously said that his interactions with her were "not unusual or unexpected" given their business ties.
Who is Alice Huang?

Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was a senior executive at Megaspeed. The Singapore-based data center company was spun off from a Chinese company in 2023, and it rents out computing power from Nvidia chips.
The Wall Street Journal reported that she and Huang were photographed together in Taipei in 2024 and 2025.
According to the Times, a memo circulated among senior US officials this spring cited intelligence that she was an asset of China's ministry of state security.
The memo said she had been recruited to gather information on Huang and possibly to steer Nvidia toward pushing for its top chips to be sold in China.
The Journal said that authorities in Singapore and Taiwan also suspected Chinese intelligence had recruited her after learning of her closeness to Huang. Her current whereabouts are unclear.
US officials suspect Megaspeed of helping smuggle restricted chips into China and the justice department has taken over a federal investigation into the company.
Megaspeed has previously described itself as a "compliant and legitimate company."
Beijing rejected the allegations. Foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said Monday that "the narrative of a so-called Chinese spy is entirely baseless vilification and smearing."
Why does it matter?

Nvidia controls an estimated 90% of the market for the chips used to train and run AI models. Washington has restricted sales of the most advanced ones to China since 2022 under the Biden administration.
Huang has also been one of Trump’s most influential informal advisers on AI.
The Journal reported that intelligence officials suspected the affair while Huang was lobbying the White House to allow chip exports to China.
Late last year, he pushed to sell Nvidia's most powerful chips there, an effort that secretary of state Marco Rubio and other officials blocked.
Trump instead allowed sales of a less advanced chip, with the US government taking a 25% cut.
According to the Times, Trump was briefed on the intelligence roughly a year ago and did not act on it.

On Fox News on Sunday, Trump was asked whether Huang should remain CEO. "I think so, oh yeah, sure,” he said, calling Huang "an honorable guy." Trump said he did not regret not acting on the intelligence.
What is the board doing?
Nvidia's board on Sunday said it had opened an independent probe into the matter.
"While the board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the board's inquiry will examine all available information," it said.
According to the Times, a committee of independent directors working with outside counsel will lead the review, and Huang will remain CEO in the meantime.
What comes next?
Republican House committee leaders, including those on the Select Committee on China, have asked Huang to attend a closed-door briefing on Nvidia's security protocols in Washington on Nov 18.

Analyst Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives predicted the episode would lead to multiple congressional inquiries. He said Huang would likely keep his job in the near term but could be ousted depending on the internal inquiry's findings.
George Chen of The Asia Group told AFP it would be "premature to conclude that Jensen poses a threat to US national security before the facts are fully established."

e7638e3da9248566: From Ibrahim M Ahmad
The delay in implementing Najib Razak's house arrest has sparked a heated debate, particularly over whether the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC) is defying a royal decree.
Yet the more consequential legal question may lie elsewhere.
Beyond the dispute over implementation is the issue of how the move could affect the calculation and enforcement of Najib's existing prison sentences.
What happens if Najib is transferred home today, only for the courts to spend years hearing arguments over whether his SRC International sentence had already ended?
A few words in a court document could affect not only Najib's treatment under the royal decree, but also when his next prison sentence begins.
Unless clarified now, the dispute could open the floodgates to further litigation.
Two sentences, one important date
Najib is serving a prison sentence in the SRC International case, scheduled to end on Aug 23, 2028.
In the separate 1MDB case, he received another 15-year sentence, which remains subject to appeal.
The court ordered the 1MDB sentence to begin only after the SRC sentence ends.
Under the existing arrangement, that means Aug 23, 2028.
The problem with 'discharge'
On Nov 6, Najib paid his fine, following which a court document was issued containing the words "discharge forthwith".
In ordinary language, that means immediate release.
But releasing someone from a prison sentence is different from transferring that person to serve the same sentence at home.
Under house arrest, Najib would remain a prisoner. Only the location of his detention would change.
The confusion appears to have arisen because this unusual situation is not expressly governed by existing written law.
The court registry appears to have applied provisions governing the discharge of prisoners to a situation those provisions were not intended to cover.
Najib's situation involves a royal decree concerning where he serves the remainder of his prison sentence, rather than its termination.
Whether the discharge procedure was legally appropriate is a question only the court can decide.
But the significance of that question extends beyond the implementation of house arrest.
If the meaning of the discharge order remains unresolved, it could have implications for the commencement and enforcement of Najib's separate 1MDB sentence.
The risk of future disputes
Consider what could happen if Najib is transferred home without clarification.
An argument could subsequently be made that the discharge order ended his SRC sentence on Nov 6, 2026.
If accepted, could his 1MDB sentence then be treated as having started that day instead of Aug 23, 2028?
That is almost two years earlier.
Could Najib also argue that time spent under house arrest should count towards his 1MDB sentence?
These are not automatic consequences, nor is there evidence that Najib's lawyers intend to pursue such arguments.
But the possibility creates uncertainty.
The courts could face further applications and appeals over when one sentence ended, when the next began and how time served should be calculated.
The 1MDB judge refused a stay
The uncertainty becomes more significant when viewed alongside developments in the 1MDB case.
The High Court rejected Najib's application for a stay of execution of his 15-year sentence pending appeal.
The judge found that Najib had not demonstrated the special circumstances necessary to justify suspending the sentence.
Unless a higher court decides otherwise, that sentence remains enforceable once his SRC sentence ends.
But if the discharge order were interpreted as ending the SRC sentence on Nov 6, would the 1MDB sentence become enforceable immediately?
Could Najib then argue that he had already begun serving his 1MDB sentence while under house arrest?
The refusal of a stay does not itself prevent Najib from serving the remainder of his SRC sentence at home.
However, would the High Court in the 1MDB case have deferred the commencement of Najib's prison sentence if the house arrest was in place when the sentence was handed down?
What Najib's lawyers acknowledge
In their latest statement, Najib's lawyers acknowledged that paying a fine does not, by itself, end a prison sentence.
This is consistent with Section 283(1)(e) of the Criminal Procedure Code.
Paying a fine removes imprisonment imposed for failing to pay it. It does not automatically cancel the original prison sentence.
On that interpretation, Najib's SRC sentence continues until Aug 23, 2028.
However, his lawyers have reserved his legal position concerning the overall effect of the royal pardon and his sentence.
That does not establish any intention to challenge the commencement date of the 1MDB sentence, but reinforces the need for judicial clarification.
Respecting the royal decree
The AGC maintains that it does not dispute the royal decree concerning Najib's house arrest.
The question is how to implement it correctly.
Seeking clarification from the court does not necessarily mean challenging the king's authority.
A clear ruling would help ensure the royal decree is implemented without affecting Najib's other sentence or drawing the monarchy into further legal controversy.
Only the courts can decide
Najib is a convicted prisoner. His sentence was imposed by the courts, and its legal consequences must be judicially determined.
His lawyers are entitled to make submissions, and the AGC may present its position. But the outcome cannot be negotiated between the parties.

The court should clarify whether the SRC sentence continues until Aug 23, 2028, whether payment of the fine affected only imprisonment in default of payment, and when the 1MDB sentence legally begins.
It should also consider the existing refusal to suspend the 1MDB sentence.
Once these questions are judicially determined, the relevant authorities can implement the decision.
Preventing a bigger problem
There is an understandable desire to implement the royal decree without delay.
But speed should not come at the expense of legal certainty.
Najib remains a prisoner whether detained at Kajang Prison or under house arrest. A short delay for clarification would not, by itself, extend his sentence.
Proceeding without clarification, however, could trigger years of litigation involving two criminal sentences and existing judicial decisions.
The purpose of clarification is not to frustrate the royal decree, but to ensure that it is implemented correctly.
A judicial ruling today could prevent years of legal arguments tomorrow.
That is preferable to allowing one disputed word to open the floodgates to further litigation.
Ibrahim M Ahmad is an FMT reader.

6709dafbb6defb4a: France has turned up the heat on Iran over destructive cyberattacks targeting refrigeration controllers at more than 700 grocery stores in October, spoiling food and sparking fires. The country vowed to take action using “all available means of response.”

The supermarket attacks, which affected Casino, Leclerc, Coopérative U, Metro, Carrefour, and Intermarché groups, started at least 15 fires and caused food losses in the tens of millions of euros, according to a Monday report by France’s Cyber Crisis Coordination Centre (C4).

The C4 includes the National Cybersecurity Agency of France, the Directorate General for External Security, the Directorate General for Internal Security, the Directorate General for Armament, and the Cyber Defence Command.

“This is an unprecedented campaign in terms of its scale and level of aggressiveness, thus constituting the first cyber offensive campaign carried out purely for the purpose of sabotage on national territory,” France’s Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs said in a statement.

Both the report and the statement attributed the refrigeration controller hacks to the Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ (IRGC) Shahid Kaveh cyber unit. The Shahid Kaveh unit, which French national security officials say is led by Reza Salarvand and Mahdi Lashgarian, is better known by its hacktivist personas, including CyberAv3ngers.

This is the same crew suspected of involvement in the July attacks that targeted more than 100 internet-exposed water systems in America. While the US government hasn’t attributed the intrusions to any country or group, private-sector security analysts blamed Iran, and specifically CyberAv3ngers.

The IRGC-affiliated hacking crew has been breaking into industrial controllers for years, and in 2023, American national security and law enforcement agencies attributed a series of cyberattacks against "multiple" US water facilities to CyberAv3ngers.

“The Iranian cyber threat against French interests is not new,” according to the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs. “Iran has already carried out several destabilizing acts against us, notably targeting the weekly magazine Charlie Hebdo in 2023 and the organization of the Paris Olympic Games in 2024.”

Since at least June 2024, the Shahid Kaveh unit has had the ability to scan, access, and control industrial control equipment from Schneider Electric, Siemens, and Rockwell, the French government said in its report. It pins the refrigeration controller hacks on this particular Iranian crew for a couple of reasons.

First: the infrastructure used to carry out the October supermarket attacks was also used during this timeframe to conduct reconnaissance on Schneider Electric equipment, zeroing in on small- and medium-sized energy and water production units. “The techniques used during these actions are known to have been used by the Shahid Kaveh unit since at least April 2026,” the report says.

It also notes that investigators found “traces of Farsi use” in the attack infrastructure. Plus, Iranian media outlet CyberbanNews, which is reportedly linked to the Shahid Kaveh unit, publicized the incidents that occurred late on October 11 and into October 12 extremely quickly: “as early as October 13.”

In early November, similar cyberattacks on commercial refrigerators and freezers were reported across Europe, with grocery stores in Belgium, Ireland, Luxembourg, and Sweden reporting widespread food losses after miscreants spiked temperatures to as high as 122°F (50°C).
Last week, the US federal government urged owners and operators to take security measures to prevent these types of attacks from spreading to America.

The French government, for its part, said that it would “use all available means of response, including within the European Union and alongside its European and international partners, to anticipate, prevent, deter and respond to destabilizing and destructive actions targeting it in cyberspace.”

This includes proposing additional EU sanctions against Iranian entities and individuals involved. France also vowed to express “its strongest condemnation of these cyberattacks” to the Iranian ambassador.

However, the country didn’t rule out responding with more than just harsh words: “France reserves the right to take any additional measures, public and non-public, deemed necessary and proportionate to respond to these cyberattacks.” ®

The person in line next to the 6-year-old “recalled the father waking his daughter up before he left and advised her he was ‘taking the dogs home,’” the report said. “Following this, [he] recalled hearing the father ask the daughter if ‘she had the gun’ before leaving.’ All parties on scene advised that the offender did not ask anyone to care or look after his daughter, and all stated the offender simply left her there by herself.”

The cops woke the girl up and she told them “she was at Target in line to get Pokémon cards with her father when the store opened,” according to the incident report. The police didn’t find a gun. “The only items the juvenile had in her possession when she was located was a pillow and a green blanket.”

Dooley returned to the line to find police talking to his daughter. “The juvenile still was unsure to the whereabouts of her father at this time,” the report said. “Several minutes after this, I could hear and see a dark colored SUV driving in the parking lot of Target in our direction. As the vehicle got closer, the [person who called 911] yelled out ‘That`s him.’”

Dooley got out of his car and police arrested him. “The offender was brought back to my patrol vehicle at which point he continued to say that he had only left to bring his dogs home,” the report said. “The offender reiterated this several times while also confirming that he left his 6-year-old daughter unattended for a period of time.” Dooley has been charged with unlawful conduct toward a child.
